agents.report:
**BioNTech (BNTX): the screen's weakness has no new bad news behind it. The stock is drifting down on a muted-catalyst, post-earnings, post-analyst-cut tape.**

**Caveat on sources.** The search tool's date tags were unreliable. Several items could not be dated and I flag them below. I read the company's Q3 press release directly. Most other facts come from secondary summaries, not the original filings.

**What I found in the news for the last two weeks.** I found nothing dated Nov 12-19 that explains today's low. The only same-day item is an AAII page. It showed $83.41 at 9:31 AM CT, a prior close of $83.26, November down 5.4% and year-to-date down 12.4%. It also said no analyst rating changes in the past month. Its headline ("down 8.79%") contradicts its own body. That mismatch looks like a template error.

**Price path, from sources**
- Nov 6 close: $87.51.
- Nov 11: about $87.73.
- November range: $82.66 to $91.46.
- Today: $82.52, slightly below the prior close.
- Bottom line: a slow bleed of about 6% in a week after the Q3 print.

**Q3 results (Nov 3, company press release)**
- Revenue was €1,289.2M, down from €1,518.9M. Weaker COVID vaccine demand drove the drop.
- IFRS net profit was €184.5M, compared with a €28.7M loss a year earlier.
  - €613M of Q3 revenue was recognized from the Bristol Myers Squibb (BMS) pumitamig partnership.
  - Year-to-date IFRS net loss is €1.17B.
- 2026 revenue guidance was narrowed up at the low end, to €1.7-1.9B from €1.6-1.9B.
  - This is still well below the €2.0-2.3B given in March. That cut is why the stock fell about 17-21% on Mar 10.
- R&D guidance is €2.0-2.3B adjusted and SG&A is €700-800M. Both are unchanged.
- Cash and investments were €16.2B on Sep 30. That is roughly equal to most of the market value.
  - My rough estimate puts the market cap near $20B, based on about 240M ADS-equivalents. That is my arithmetic, not a sourced figure.
- The buyback is up to $1B through May 6, 2027. Through Sep 30, $463M had been used (5.04M ADSs). It is a real, ongoing bid under the stock.
- Restructuring costs of €223M were excluded from adjusted results, with impairments on assets outside the strategic focus. A €13.5M legal item was also excluded.
- BioNTech exercised an option with Roche/Genentech. From Jan 1, 2027, future R&D costs on that program generally go to Roche, with possible royalties for BioNTech. The release does not name the program.

**Analysts after the print**
- H.C. Wainwright cut its target to $110 from $130 and kept Buy.
- Morgan Stanley cut to $106 from $114 and kept Overweight (year not confirmed on the page).
- Bank of America is at $108.
- BMO downgraded to Market Perform in September, with a target of $105. The stock was at $102.55 then.
- Targets sit about 30% above the price. The market is clearly not buying them.

**Pipeline and catalysts**
- **Pumitamig (BNT327), PD-L1xVEGF bispecific, partnered with BMS.** It is the core of the equity story, with seven pivotal trials running.
  - Oct 25 ROSETTA Lung-107 Phase 2 data: 36.7% confirmed response rate in 30 evaluable patients (docetaxel combination, second line after immunotherapy plus chemo). Median progression-free survival (PFS) was 6.9 months across 50 treated patients. No drug-related deaths.
  - A Phase 3 in triple-negative breast cancer with Gilead's sacituzumab govitecan is pending regulatory approval.
  - No Phase 3 readout is confirmed in the next 10 sessions.
  - Competitors: Summit/Akeso's ivonescimab is the key read-through. Its HARMONi-3 squamous final PFS is expected in the second half of 2026, and non-squamous in the first half of 2027. A global trial missed its overall survival goal in May 2025.
  - Other rivals: Pfizer (from 3SBio), and Merck's MK-2010 (early data).
  - A Summit HARMONi-3 result or an ivonescimab regulatory event could swing BNTX in either direction. I could not date any such event.
- **Gotistobart (BNT316), an anti-CTLA-4 antibody.** This is the nearest binary event.
  - The first interim analysis of the Phase 3 PRESERVE-003 pivotal stage is expected "toward the end of 2026". The data monitoring committee will either unblind or continue.
  - Stage 1 data (Sept 2026, 87 patients): median overall survival 18.5 months versus 10.0 for docetaxel (hazard ratio 0.56, nominal p=0.0295).
  - Serious treatment-related adverse events were 44.4% versus 29.3%. The FDA placed a partial hold in October 2024 over squamous versus non-squamous differences.
  - Timing is unconfirmed, so it could land inside the window. I found no report that it has happened.
- **Trastuzumab pamirtecan (BNT323, with DualityBio).** DYNASTY-Breast02 met its PFS endpoint, but the company described the benefit as modest, with higher rates of interstitial lung disease. Talks on next steps, including a possible BLA, are ongoing, and the company will update the market.
- **BNT113 (AHEAD-MERIT, head and neck cancer).** The Phase 2/3 missed its PFS endpoint on Oct 13. The shares fell more than 5% that day.
  - The trial continues to the overall survival analysis, which could still be a win.
  - Plaintiff-firm "investigations" exist. One report (Levi & Korsinsky) is single-source, from a German site.
- **Autogene cevumeran (personalized mRNA cancer vaccine, with Genentech).** Early termination has begun in the colorectal Phase 2. The pancreatic cancer trial finished enrollment in August 2026.
- **Priority review voucher.** BioNTech agreed on Nov 10 to buy an FDA voucher from Scholar Rock for $205M cash. Closing is subject to HSR antitrust clearance. No candidate was named. Pumitamig is the speculated use. The purchase signals an intent to file with the FDA.

**Management and strategy**
- Guido Oelkers, Sobi's CEO, becomes CEO by Feb 1, 2027 (announced Aug 3).
- Co-founders Ugur Sahin and Özlem Türeci leave by the end of 2026 to start a separate next-generation mRNA company.
  - Türeci's CMO successor has not been found. No details on the new company or on a financial link to BioNTech.
- In May, BioNTech announced exits from German and Singapore manufacturing sites, with up to 1,860 jobs affected.
- This is a pivot from COVID vaccines to oncology. The new CEO's goal is multiple approved products by 2030, and he may change course.

**Overhangs**
- **COVID vaccine:** The XFG-adapted vaccine was approved in Europe in July. The FDA approved it in August for ages 65 and up, and 5-64 with a risk condition. The US policy tone toward mRNA remains hostile. I could not date any November ACIP action.
- **Patents:**
  - The UK Court of Appeal ruled for Moderna on EP 949 (valid and infringed). BioNTech and Pfizer can seek a Supreme Court appeal.
  - A Düsseldorf court ordered disclosure of sales and profit data, with reasonable compensation due. A European Patent Office appeal was set for September 2026, and I did not find its outcome.
  - On Nov 10, Arbutus/Genevant added a newly granted lipid-nanoparticle patent to its Canadian suit against Pfizer and BioNTech, and sued in other countries in July. These are procedural steps with no damages figure.
  - BioNTech countersued Moderna over mNEXSPIKE in Delaware in February.
  - BioNTech and Pfizer won against Promosome at the Unified Patent Court (Munich) in July.

**Read for a 1-10 session trade**
- **Technical picture:** The stock is below its 52-week closing low of $83.26, below both falling moving averages, and on 4.1 times normal volume. The 52-week intraday low of $79.52 is only 3.6% below. A break below $79.52 would be a new low with no obvious support underneath.
- **Why the setup looks like fundamentals-driven drift:** I found no negative announcement on Nov 18-19. A decline on high volume with no news is typical of post-earnings repositioning, tax-loss selling or a sector move. I did not find which of these it is.
- **What supports the stock:** Cash is a large share of the market value, and the buyback is active. A catalyst could land at any time: the gotistobart interim (late 2026, date unconfirmed), HARMONi-3 squamous, or the BNT323 BLA decision.
- **What weighs on it:** Revenue is shrinking, the oncology pivot has no approved product, there is a leadership vacuum with Sahin and Türeci leaving, mRNA policy is hostile, and recent trial news was mixed (a miss on BNT113, a modest result on BNT323, and a "continue" call on gotistobart is possible).
- **Binary risk:** A gotistobart unblinding would be a large upside move. A "continue" decision or a negative read from ivonescimab could push the stock to new lows.

**Gaps.** I did not confirm what drove the Nov 12-19 slide or today's volume. I did not confirm the Summit HARMONi-3 status or any November ACIP/FDA action. I did not find Q3 ADS-level EPS on a consistent basis.

agents.report:
**Corteva (CTVA): research for the 1-10 session decision, Thursday 2026-11-19, about 9:00 AM CT**

CTVA is a crop-protection company that fell hard after a bad first standalone quarter, and the selling now looks like a business reset rather than a spin-off artifact. Two of the screen's numbers are distorted by the spin-off (see "Corrections to the screen").

**Corrections to the screen**
- On Oct 1, 2026 Corteva spun off its seed business as Vylor (VYLR), one Vylor share per Corteva share. CTVA fell about 84% that day, from $77.65 to $12.56. That was a mechanical transfer of value, not a loss.
- CTVA is now "New Corteva", crop protection only, with about 667M shares. It dropped out of the S&P 500 and moved to the S&P MidCap 400.
- The 200-day average ($12.04) and the 36% 20-day decline are probably contaminated by this reset. The real post-spin damage is the Nov 12 earnings drop plus the slide since.
- The "prior 52-week low of $8.35" is a post-spin price. MarketBeat reports the low was set around Nov 18-19, and $8.23 is now below it.

**What happened**
- **Nov 12 earnings (first standalone report):** Shares fell about 20% that day, from $12.14 to $9.74, with an intraday low of $9.14. (One source says 24%, another 22%.) Q3 net sales were $2.46B (down 6%) and adjusted pro forma EPS was $0.06 against $0.14 a year earlier. Pro forma operating EBITDA for crop protection was $222M against a $268M adjusted figure a year ago.
- **Guidance cut:** 2026 operating EBITDA is now $1.10-1.125B, down from about $1.3B given at the September investor day (roughly 12% lower). Management attributed the entire cut to Brazil, roughly $200M. About half is channel inventory and volume, and the rest is price. Second-half EBITDA guidance fell from about $579M to about $397M.
  - Management said Brazil "worsened considerably" in the last two weeks of September.
  - Latin America volume fell 24% and generics caused 7% price erosion.
  - Brazil sell-out is down about 12% year to date.
  - Corteva carried about $250M of excess product into 2026, and distributors are past due. Management will not extend credit.
- **Acetochlor:** About $60M of the $120M Q3 price headwind was US acetochlor, with about $40M more expected in Q4.
- **Q4:** EBITDA is guided to about half of last year's. Sales are about $2B, with the decline almost all price. Cash is expected to fall from $1.8B to about $1.5B, and financial debt to be about $1B.
- **Management's recovery timeline:**
  - The year-over-year price decline is similar in Q4, tapers in Q1 2027 and is minimal by Q2 2027.
  - Management says growth in 2027 comes from cost and volume, but gave no number. An analyst's rough framework implied $1.11-1.15B EBITDA.
  - It will give details on the restructuring and 2027 in the Feb 2 call.
  - A third-party cost review has started, with a hiring freeze and a pause on some R&D. Management said "we simply cannot afford the infrastructure we inherited."
  - It is reassessing Brazil's long-term model, including possible exits of specific products.
  - No major molecules lose patent protection before the end of 2028.
  - New products grew 20% in volume.

**Analysts and insiders**
- Targets after the report:
  - RBC: $11 (from $17), Outperform.
  - Mizuho: $13 (from $16), Outperform. Its estimates are $1.12B EBITDA for 2026, $1.14B for 2027 and $1.24B for 2028.
  - KeyBanc: $14 (from $17), Overweight.
  - Citi: $10.30, neutral.
  - Barclays: reinstated today (Nov 19) at Equalweight, $11.
  - Oppenheimer: downgraded to Perform and dropped its target, citing execution.
- Every target is above the $8.23 price, but they are stale cuts that lag the move. The analyst consensus figures I found conflict with each other, so I would not rely on them.
- **Insider buys:** CEO Kissam bought 32,292 shares on Nov 13 (he now holds 185,379). Director Page bought 20,000 shares at about $9.27 between Nov 13 and 16.

**Valuation and dividend**
- Management says buybacks are blocked for the rest of 2026 by spin-related tax restrictions and are a 2027 priority.
- The quarterly dividend is $0.05, with an ex-dividend date of Dec 1. That is $0.20 a year, about 2.4% at $8.23.
- Some aggregators show an 8.6% or 7.6% yield based on pre-spin payouts. Those are wrong, so ignore them.
- Forward EPS of $0.76-0.80 at $8.23 is roughly 10-11x, and EV/EBITDA is roughly 5x (my estimate, from market cap of about $5.5B, net debt of roughly zero and EBITDA of $1.1B).

**Risks**
- Brazil is a structural problem (generic competition, grower credit stress, high rates, El Niño, currency) and not only a destocking issue.
- A Q4 EBITDA halving is already guided. There is no scheduled catalyst before Feb 2.
- Legacy PFAS liabilities remain. They are shared with DuPont and Chemours, with some "stray liability" fallback to Corteva, and public-nuisance claims are still open. I found no source on how the post-spin allocation works.
- Seed-side lawsuits (states sued to block the spin) matter more for Vylor.
- Tax-selling and index-selling pressure is plausible after the S&P 500 exit and the spin, but I found no source documenting it.

**Read for a 1-10 session trade**
- The story is a real fundamental reset, not a mechanical artifact. Management has pre-announced a bad Q4 and a plan, with insiders buying near $9.3 and cheap multiples as the rebound case.
- The case against is no turn yet, a stock still making new lows after the reset, and no catalyst for months. Today's volume so far is light, and the drop continued after the Nov 12 low, so the selling had not exhausted as of Nov 18-19.
- A bounce is possible from the oversold reading, but the story gives no near-term reason for one. Treat it as a technical mean-reversion trade at most, with a tight stop below the new low. I found no news dated Nov 19 beyond the Barclays reinstatement.

**Caveats**
- Several figures come from secondary summaries (AI-assisted transcript, aggregators) that conflict with each other. I did not open the Q3 8-K release or the 10-Q directly.
- The Nov 12 move was reported as 19.77%, 22% or 24% depending on the source.
- The pro forma EPS figures vary by source: $0.06 adjusted in the RTT piece, while the pro forma statement shows a loss.

agents.report:
FMS has a clear negative story and no turn yet. The latest leg down looks like sector and supply pressure on top of a deteriorating earnings outlook, not a company-specific shock. I could not confirm the cause of today's 2% drop or of DaVita's 6.5% drop on Nov 18. I did not find a 2027 guidance date other than February. The Q3 figures come from the company's own release and the earnings call transcript. The rest comes from secondary sources, noted below.

**The story**
- **Q3 (Nov 3):** Revenue was EUR 4.94B, flat at constant currency. Adjusted operating income fell 5% to EUR 545M (margin 11.0% vs 11.7%). Reported net income fell 42% on China exit costs (EUR 108M). Adjusted EPS was flat.
- **Guidance:** The 2026 operating income outlook was narrowed to the lower half of its range, flat to down mid-single digits. Q4 carries a TDAPA headwind of about EUR 140M (TDAPA is the temporary add-on Medicare payment for new dialysis drugs). Management said inflation headwinds will exceed its earlier EUR 300M estimate, citing energy and logistics costs.
- **2027 is the main worry.** Management flagged a EUR 300-350M operating income headwind versus 2026, company-wide, and analysts were surprised by its size. CMS's 2027 rate update is 1.9% base and 3.5% for dialysis clinics, but 3.1 points of that is TDAPA-related, leaving about 0.4% for inflation. There is no formal 2027 guidance until February.
- **Volumes:** US same-market treatment growth was -1.1% in Q3 and is guided to about -0.9% for the year. Management says patient inflow has stabilized to the prior-year level but that recovery takes several quarters, with flu season the Q4 risk. It rejects the idea that the weakness is structural. The ACA enrollment headwind (EUR 50M in 2026) is not yet quantified for 2027.
- **Cash and capital:** Free cash flow was EUR 564M for the quarter and leverage is 2.6x. A EUR 1B buyback is running, with 9.1M shares (3.4%) bought through Sept 30 and the first tranche ending mid-December. Management said buybacks will be weighed against reinvestment.
- **Management:** Shervin Korangy became CEO on Oct 12, three weeks before the call, and his strategy is still being developed. The company also cited FDA audit findings being addressed.
- **Value-Based Care (its managed-care contract business):** Revenue fell 9% but operating income reached breakeven. The company's goal is to break even in 2026.

**Recent catalysts**
- **Aug 4 (Q2):** The stock fell about 8% on weak US volumes even though results beat estimates. A May 5 gap down of about 10% came on multiple downgrades. A MarketBeat summary shows a "Reduce" consensus, with Hold and Sell ratings and an average target of about $24. These are aggregator figures and I could not date every rating action.
- **Oct 20:** DaVita fell more than 6% (FMS also dropped) when the administration proposed a Kidney Care National Plan, reported by Seeking Alpha as HHS seeking dialysis market reforms. It aims to open the market to new entrants; the two firms hold roughly 74% of it. I could not open the article itself (403), so the details are second-hand.
- **Nov 9:** A CNN page headline list says Barclays downgraded FMS to Underweight. This is unverified.
- **Nov 12 (supply):** Parent Fresenius SE sold 13.4M FMC shares at EUR 39.00, about EUR 524M and about 2.7% below the prior Xetra close. Its stake falls from about 25% to about 20%, with a 90-day lock-up on the rest. That means a possible overhang from the placement, but no further parent selling until about February.
- **Nov 18:** Berenberg kept Neutral and cut its target to EUR 37 from EUR 42 (no reasoning given). The Xetra close was EUR 38.56. The same day DaVita fell 6.5%, which likely explains FMS weakness today, but I could not confirm the reason.

**Setup read for 1-10 sessions**
- **Against a long:** There is no technical turn, and the stock is at 52-week-low territory. The 2027 headwind, the HHS reform overhang and the Berenberg cut keep sentiment bearish. The 2027 guidance clarity is months away.
- **For a bounce:** The buyback is still running through mid-December and the parent placement is done. Management says volumes are stabilizing. Valuation is cheap, but that has not been a catalyst.
- **Next scheduled events:** None found inside the 1-10 session window. Possible unscheduled items are DaVita follow-through, news on the HHS plan, and the Q4 flu-season read.

**KBR research brief, as of 9:00 AM CT, Thu 2026-11-19**

I could not find what moved the stock on Nov 16–18, when it fell from about $35.3 to $32.9. Searches turned up nothing specific. I also found no new rating changes after the investor day.

**Why it is stretched down**
- **Sell-off:** The stock closed near $38.65 on Nov 9 and fell about 6.7% on Nov 11, the day of the KBR investor day, to about $36.3. It then drifted to about $35.3 by Nov 13 (one source says $35.59). It broke below its 200-day average around Nov 12.
- **No single news item explains it:** Q3 results on Oct 29 were fine. The pressure looks like a reaction to 2027 headwinds disclosed at the investor day, plus spin-off uncertainty.
- **Investor day tone:** Coverage reported the new targets but found no sign of analysts upgrading on them.

**Q3 results (Oct 29, reaffirmed guidance)**
- **Headline numbers:** Revenue was $2.03B (+5%) and missed consensus. Adjusted EBITDA was $268M (+12%, 13.2% margin) and beat. Adjusted EPS was $1.12 (+10%).
- **Guidance:** FY26 guidance was unchanged: adjusted EPS $3.87–$4.22, adjusted EBITDA $980M–$1,040M, revenue $7.90B–$8.36B, adjusted operating cash flow $560M–$600M.
- **Sustainable Technology Solutions (STS):** Revenue rose 26% to $762M and backlog hit a record $5.8B (+50%). Book-to-bill was 1.3x. Margin slipped to 19.3% from 21.2% because of the lower-margin LNG joint venture; excluding it, margin was 13.9%.
- **Mission Technology Solutions (MTS):** Revenue was down 5% (the call summary says 1%; the press release is the primary source). Book-to-bill was 0.6x because of NASA insourcing "debooking" and delayed procurement. Q4 is guided flat to slightly down.
- **Cash flow:** Operating cash flow was $171M (-14%). Nine-month operating cash flow was $331M versus $506M a year earlier. Management said $25M–$50M of cash collections could slip past year-end because of Middle East payment delays.
- **Buybacks:** None in Q3, versus $100M a year earlier.
- **Balance sheet:** Net leverage is 2.1x, and liquidity is about $1.1B. The dividend is small, with ex-dividend on Dec 15.
- **Settlement:** KBR settled the TRANSCOM household-goods contract dispute, converting a termination for default to termination for convenience.

**Investor day (Nov 11): KBR standalone after the spin**
- **Targets:** Organic revenue growth of 10%+ a year over 2026–2029, excluding megaprojects. Adjusted EBITDA margin of 12%+ for 2027–2029 and free cash flow conversion of 85%+. Net leverage below 2.5x. Management called these objectives, not guidance, and gave no EPS target.
- **Scale:** One outlet put revenue at about $2.9B in 2026, rising to about $3.85B in 2029. Adjusted EBITDA is expected above $425M in 2027.
- **2027 headwind:** The wind-down of the Plaquemines LNG joint venture removes about $100M of EBITDA. It contributes about $140M in 2026 and falls to roughly $40M–$50M in 2027.
- **Pipeline:** The qualified pipeline is $54B, and more than 75% of revenue comes from existing customers.

**Spin-off and Trinzic (formerly MTS)**
- **Timing:** The spin-off is targeted for Jan 4, 2027, subject to board approval and the Form 10 becoming effective. Management expected a tax-free-treatment ruling and Trinzic's debt launch in mid-November; I did not confirm either.
- **Trinzic scale:** It starts with about $5.1B of revenue and a 9.5% adjusted EBITDA margin. It targets 3%–6% growth and a margin above 9% through 2029.
- **Trinzic risks:** NASA insourcing is a roughly $200M (about 4%) revenue headwind in 2027. The growth target excludes it. About 83% of revenue is U.S. government.
- **Antarctica contract:** The $8B Antarctic contract was re-awarded after a protest pause, and work is under way.
- **Spin-off flows:** Spin-offs often produce forced selling and index-driven selling around the distribution. This is my inference, not something I found in a source.

**Analysts**
- **Consensus:** Consensus is Hold, with an average target around $44.8 (three Buy, five Hold, per MarketBeat). Wells Fargo raised its target to $40 from $35 after earnings, keeping Equal Weight.
- **Cuts:** Oppenheimer and Citigroup trimmed targets, per a MarketBeat roundup; I could not confirm the details.
- **History:** Several downgrades to neutral in 2025 (Goldman, UBS, BofA, KeyBanc). Truist cut its target in Dec 2025 on the Lake Charles LNG suspension.

**Read for a 1–10 session trade**
- **For a bounce:**
  - The stock is oversold (RSI 31) and at a 52-week range low end.
  - Guidance was reaffirmed.
  - STS growth and backlog are strong.
  - Leverage is moderate.
  - The share price is well below the $40–$45 analyst targets.
- **Against a bounce:**
  - The sell-off has no clear catalyst, so it is hard to say what ends it.
  - It sits just under the 20-day low and below both moving averages, with volatility 1.6x normal.
  - The 2027 LNG and NASA headwinds are now known and weigh on near-term estimates.
  - There are no buybacks.
  - Spin-off supply pressure could build into the January date.
- **Upcoming catalysts:** The Form 10 effectiveness, Trinzic's debt launch, and the distribution record date. I did not find these dates. Possible negatives are further analyst target cuts and any news on a NASA contract.
- **Bottom line:** There is no broken thesis, but the weakness has no identified end. Entering looks like a mean-reversion bet that depends on price confirming a turn, for example a reclaim of the $33.05 level.

Searching has stopped turning up new material, so here is the picture. I could not read today's call transcript. It was not yet available when I searched, and the call may not have started at 8:55 AM CT.

## Why it is down
- **Prior close and trigger.** The stock closed Wednesday at $260.09, up 4.0% on no company news, helped by a retail bounce after TJX (+8%) and Target (+4%) reported. That put the stock near its highs going into earnings. Pre-market it was down about 7%, to around $242, which matches your $242.43.
- **The quarter was in line, not a miss.** Q3 (ended Nov 1) revenue was $1.991B, up 5.8%, against about $2.00B expected. Non-GAAP EPS was $2.19 against $2.18 to $2.21 expected, up 11.7%. Comparable brand revenue rose 5.1%, against 4.0% a year ago. Every brand had a positive comp. Source: [Q3 press release](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/719955/000071995526000244/exhibit991fy2026q3earnings.htm).
- **The sell-off looks like "priced for a beat, got in line."** [StockStory](https://stockstory.org/us/stocks/nyse/wsm/news/earnings/williams-sonoma-reports-q3-2026-in-line-with-expectations-but-stock-drops) attributes the drop to that. Seeking Alpha and [Newsquawk](https://www.newsquawk.com/headlines/daily-us-equity-opening-news-ant-ipo-priced-at-83shr-panw-rallies-on-earnings-beat-wmt-slips-on-comp-sales-miss) both read it as a slight revenue miss. The 4% pre-earnings run-up made the bar higher.

## Details that matter
- **Brand split.** West Elm comped +7.0% and Williams Sonoma +6.8%. Pottery Barn, the largest brand at $763M, comped only +1.8%. Pottery Barn Kids and Teen comped +2.9%, down from +4.4% a year ago.
- **Margins.** GAAP gross margin was 47.6%, up 150 bps, but 140 bps of that came from IEEPA tariff refunds. Non-GAAP gross margin was 46.2%, up only 10 bps. Non-GAAP operating margin was 17.4%, up 40 bps. Higher oil-related supply chain costs took away about 50 bps.
- **Refunds.** Substantially all of the $197.8M refund claim has been collected, so there is little left to flatter results.
- **Cash and buybacks.** Q3 buybacks were $163M and dividends $90M. Cash is $992M, and inventory is $1.64B, up 7.3% against revenue up 5.8%.
- **Free cash flow margin.** StockStory puts it at 10.8%, down from 13.2%.
- **Guidance reiterated, not raised.** FY26 net revenue is +4.7% to +7.2%, comps +4.0% to +6.5%, and non-GAAP operating margin 17.8% to 18.2%. The company will give FY27 guidance in March.
- **The Q4 margin ramp.** Year-to-date non-GAAP operating margin is 17.0%, so hitting 17.8% to 18.2% needs a stronger Q4. That is my inference, and the market may be doubting it.
- **What the Q2 call said about Q4.** Management said Q2 was the peak tariff margin hit and that it laps tariffs from mid-Q3 and fully in Q4. Q4 also has to lap a roughly 150 bps shrink-accrual benefit from last year, which offsets some of that relief. Source: [Q2 call summary](https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/08/31/williams-sonoma-wsm-q2-2026-earnings-call-transcript/).
- **Housing assumption.** Guidance assumes no housing recovery and no change in interest rates.
- **Oil assumption.** Guidance assumes oil stays elevated. Oil fell about 3% Wednesday, but there are Strait of Hormuz tanker and supply headlines today.

## Backdrop
- **Rates.** The Fed's October minutes said "almost all participants" see further hikes as likely appropriate. Markets price about 90% odds of a December 8-9 hike, and JPMorgan expects three hikes. That is a headwind for housing-linked names. Source: [Coffee Grounds newsletter](https://coffeegroundstrading.substack.com/p/the-coffee-grounds-newsletter-november-5e3).
- **Market tape.** The S&P 500 had five straight down days, then futures were up about 1.2% pre-market on Palo Alto's beat. WSM falling 7% against that tape is stock-specific.
- **Walmart.** It beat and raised but slipped on a slight comp miss, so "good but not enough" is the pattern today.
- **Tariffs.**
  - Section 232 duties on upholstered furniture and cabinets stay at 25%, with the step-ups delayed to January 1, 2027. That is a looming risk.
  - A new Section 301 tariff was announced July 23, and guidance assumes it stays.
  - IEEPA tariffs are no longer part of the picture, since they have been refunded.

Stifel initiated at Buy with a $290 target. Telsey is at $285 with Outperform. Citi is at $275 with Neutral. Barclays is at $240 with Equal Weight.

- **Bull case.** The business is steady: six-plus quarters of positive comps, broad brand strength, strong cash flow, and buybacks. The gap-down is a valuation and expectation reset on a clean in-line print. The 50-day ($243.46) and the 20-day low ($242.81) are being tested, and the 200-day ($216.61) is well below.

agents.report:
**Managed care (UNH, HUM, ELV, CNC, MOH, OSCR, CI): research as of 9:00 AM CT, Thu 2026-11-19**

**Bottom line:** The weakness is a policy shock, not a fundamentals break. A proposed CMS rule (called CRUSH) landed Monday 11-16, and the group sold off hard on Tuesday and Wednesday. Q3 earnings were mostly good. The legal and political odds of the rule surviving look weak, but the downside if it does survive is large. I found no source covering today's trading, premarket or regular session.

**1. The catalyst: the CRUSH proposed rule**
- CMS posted it Monday 11-16 as CMS-6098-P, short for "Comprehensive Regulations to Uncover Suspicious Healthcare". It was due to publish in the Federal Register today, 11-19, with comments due 1-19-2027.
- The provision that matters is Medicare Advantage RADV (risk-adjustment data validation audits).
  - It would codify extrapolating audit findings, starting with payment year 2018, with no fee-for-service adjuster.
  - CMS estimates about $9B recovered per payment year. It also cites roughly $90B of federal savings over 2027-2036 across Medicare, Medicaid and ACA.
  - One source reads the $90.2B figure as the transfer from MA plans to the government if extrapolation applies.
- Other provisions: mandatory fraud reporting by MA and Part D plans, a requirement that MA-billing providers be enrolled in Original Medicare, a 60-day overpayment-return rule in Medicaid fee-for-service, and ACA broker safeguards.
- CMS says it intends to issue similar rules annually.
- The sources don't size any single insurer's share of the clawback.

**2. Price action, from secondary sources. Figures conflict on exact numbers and dates.**
- **Tuesday 11-17:** UNH closed at $389.68, down about 5.4%, from $412.02. HUM fell about 4.3%, ELV about 2.3%, MOH about 2.1% and CNC about 1.9%.
- **Wednesday 11-18:** UNH fell 10.2% to $349.91, which cut the Dow by 561 points. HUM fell 13.0% to $385.78. ELV fell 7.6%, CNC 7.0%, CVS 5.2% and CI about 3%. UNH was down about 15% and HUM about 16% over the two days.
- Mid-session figures on 11-18 had OSCR down 5.4% and MOH down 5.4%. I found no closing numbers for either.
- One 247wallst item says UNH's drop had "no clear catalyst". That conflicts with every other source and I can't resolve it.
- Our screen shows the basket down only 4.9% over five sessions, which looks small next to HUM and UNH down 15%. I can't tell whether that is index construction or a data gap. Check the screen against live quotes before trusting it.
- Today's -0.4% for the basket at 8:50 AM CT means little against moves of that size on the two prior days.

**3. Why the stocks fell by different amounts**
- **UNH:** Medicare premiums were 44% of 2025 revenue. It is the most exposed in dollars, and it was already under DOJ scrutiny.
- **HUM:** It is the most concentrated in government programs. Extrapolation scales with MA enrollment, so exposure is proportionally highest.
  - It trades at roughly 27x forward earnings by one source's math, which leaves little cushion.
  - It reported a Q3 profit of $162M and raised 2026 adjusted EPS to at least $9.50.
  - Its 2027 Star Ratings averaged 4.17, near its best ever, with a one-time 2028 tailwind that has not been quantified.
  - Early 2027 MA enrollment is ahead of plan.
  - It has an investor update on 12-10.
- **ELV and CNC:** They carry more Medicaid and ACA exposure and less MA, so they fell less.
- **CVS (Aetna):** Exposure runs through Aetna. CVS is not in our basket.
- **MOH:** It has almost no MA business, so it is mostly a sympathy move.
- **CI:** It has little MA exposure after selling that business, so it is also mostly sympathy. A Cigna drop of about 3% was reported.

**4. The case for a bounce**
- The rule is only a proposal. Nothing is in force, and it won't affect near-term earnings.
- A federal judge in Texas (O'Connor, 9-25-2025) vacated the 2023 RADV final rule in Humana v. Becerra, on procedural grounds. The court did not rule on whether extrapolation or dropping the fee-for-service adjuster is lawful.
- CMS appealed in November 2025 and I couldn't confirm the appeal's current status. Audits were still expected to continue.
- Oppenheimer calls the selloff an overreaction, citing legal challenges and political hurdles. It notes a similar 2025 proposal was struck down in court.
- Valuation: UNH is about 17x forward earnings after the drop, against a five-year average of 19x.
- Sell-side consensus is Strong Buy on UNH and HUM, with targets of $482.69 for UNH and $508.68 for HUM. Molina and Oscar are at Hold.
- Q3 results were mostly clean, so the fundamentals went into the selloff intact:
  - **UNH (10-13):** Raised 2026 adjusted EPS to at least $20.50. The medical care ratio improved to 88.4%, helped by $610M of favorable reserve development. Commercial cost trend is above 11%.
  - **ELV:** Raised 2026 adjusted EPS to at least $29, with Medicaid expected to improve in 2027. I found this from one source only.
  - **CNC (10-27):** Raised adjusted EPS to above $5.20, and Q3 adjusted EPS was $0.58. Total membership is down to 25.7M from 27.6M at year-end 2025.
  - **CI:** Raised 2026 adjusted EPS to at least $30.60 and guides 2027 growth of at least 10%. Pharmacy benefit services income fell 22% in the quarter.

**5. The case against, and the risks**
- Morgan Stanley's range of 11% to 51% of 2028 earnings for UNH, HUM and CVS is wide, so it is not a number you can size a trade on. I couldn't find the note itself. One summary credits it with the 11%-51% range, but I couldn't confirm the year.
- If CMS fixes the procedural defects from the 2023 rule, the second attempt could survive court. The 2018 look-back creates a large one-time liability.
- UNH's operating margin was 4.8% in 2025 against 8.1% in 2024. Any repayment comes out of a thin margin.
- Last January, CMS's 2027 MA advance notice proposed only a 0.09% rate increase against 4-6% expected. UNH fell about 20% that day. The final 2027 rate is due by about 4-6-2026, and I didn't find the outcome.
- The UNH and Aetna 2027 plan designs limit provider access, which points to continued margin defense.
- **ACA exposure:** The enhanced subsidies expired at the end of 2025, and as of September 2026 Congress had not extended them.
  - KFF expects effectuated enrollment to fall by up to about 5 million.
  - Median requested 2027 premium increases are about 15%.
  - Molina is cutting its marketplace footprint from 14 states to 6. Centene is exiting Delaware and New Hampshire. Cigna is exiting the ACA.
  - Open enrollment for 2027 runs through 1-15-2027.
- **MOH:** Q3 net income fell 52% to $38M and its medical loss ratio was 92.9%. It kept its 2026 adjusted EPS floor at $5.25 and raised its cost-trend assumption to 5.5%. The stock fell about 5% after hours.
- **OSCR:** Q3 operating profit included a $250M one-time risk-adjustment benefit, and the stock fell 5.7% after earnings. Its guidance implies an operating loss in Q4 of roughly $320M-$420M. That is one analyst's calculation, not company guidance. Its stated 2027 ACA rate increase is about 14%.

**6. Catalysts over the next 1 to 10 sessions**
- Federal Register publication today and the early comment-letter flow. Heavy insurer and provider opposition would point to a lawsuit.
- Any company statement sizing its exposure. UNH's 2027 outlook is expected before year-end.
- Humana's 12-10 investor update.
- Any congressional or legal response to the rule.
- Analyst upgrades or downgrades. I found none yet.

**7. For the screen read**
- The basket is oversold and the screen shows no turn. The cause is a headline-driven repricing of a proposal, not a change in earnings.
- The rule is a multi-month story with real tail risk. A bounce is plausible if it only reverses the headline, but a second leg down is also plausible if a company sizes its exposure badly.
- The spread across names is probably wide, with HUM and UNH most exposed to the rule and MOH, OSCR and CI mostly moving in sympathy. Single-name risk matters more than basket risk.
- Everything above comes from secondary news sites, some of them AI-written summaries. I couldn't open the CMS rule text, the company releases or SEC filings directly. Verify prices against your quote feed.

**Greif (GEF) research, 9:00 AM CT Thursday 2026-11-19**

**Short version:** The selloff is a slow bleed from an earnings disappointment, not a single shock. The stock gapped down on the November 3 report and kept sliding. No new negative company news turned up since, and the next report is 2027-01-26. The oversold reading looks like an earnings reset plus soft industrial demand, not a broken business. Nothing I found marks a turning point.

**Price path (sources are inconsistent; treat the figures as approximate)**
- About $80 in mid-October, around the Raymond James upgrade.
- $81.25 close before the report on November 3.
- Opened near $74.80 on the gap down, closing down roughly 5.6% by one account. The stock then broke below its 200-day average.
- $72.52 on November 10, $70.98 on November 16, $67.49 close on November 18. Your $66.73 fits this path.
- Several sites list a 52-week low near $58–60 and a high near $90.

**The earnings report (fiscal Q4 2026, released November 3, call November 4)**
- **Miss:** Adjusted EPS was $0.87 against about $1.09–1.12 expected. Revenue of $1.14B beat, mostly on pricing.
- **Weak EBITDA:** Adjusted EBITDA was $163.0M, down 3.1%. Excluding $18.2M of prior-year accrual timing, it was up 8.7%, a sharp slowdown from roughly 25% in the third quarter.
- **Volumes:** They turned negative again. Customized Polymer Solutions and Durable Metal Solutions volumes were each down 2.3%, and closures were down 3.5%.
- **Why volumes fell:** Management blamed destocking of small plastic containers, which it tied to high resin costs and customers waiting for resin prices to fall. A weak farm season also hurt. It called this "isolated to Q4."
- **Tone:** The CEO said there are "no convincing signs of a broad recovery." Europe is weaker.
- **Free cash flow:** Full-year adjusted free cash flow was $279.3M, below the $305–325M guided in the third quarter. Inventory and resin costs (tied to the Middle East conflict) were the cause.
- **Bright spots:**
  - Full-year adjusted EBITDA was $625.7M, up 11.7%, and adjusted EPS was $4.04, up 75%.
  - Leverage is 1.2x.
  - $225M of buybacks, about 6% of shares.
  - Cost savings of $105M run-rate, with the target raised to $150M by the end of fiscal 2027.
  - The company is closing its Sweetwater, Georgia, paperboard mill and exiting coated recycled board. That brought $36.5M of impairments and a GAAP loss of $0.11 per share.
- **Dividend:** $0.62 quarterly, about 3.5% yield, ex-dividend December 17.

**Fiscal 2027 guidance (low end, described as conservative)**
- Adjusted EBITDA of $645M, about 3% growth, and adjusted free cash flow of $290M.

agents.report:
**Bottom line:** TGB's drop is mostly a copper and macro selloff on top of a soft earnings reaction. I found no company-specific bad news since earnings on Nov 4. The business is cash-generative but still leveraged and execution-dependent. Because the move is driven by copper, the entry depends on what copper does next, which I couldn't confirm for today.

**Why the stock fell**
- **Copper fell hard on Nov 18.** COMEX copper was about $5.62/lb, down about 6% on the day, 10.6% over a week and 14.4% over a month. It is still up about 11% over a year. One report had LME copper down as much as 5.6% to its lowest since April, a seven-month low (the $12,471/t close comes from that same report, not from the COMEX page).
  - The causes given are an AI-trade unwind, a fading US refined-copper tariff premium, Fed rate-hike expectations with a stronger dollar, and a flush of speculative longs.
  - Physical tightness is still reported: a record China import premium of $360/t and low Chinese warehouse stocks. One article argues sentiment, not fundamentals, is setting the price right now.
  - Two of the copper articles are AI-generated, so treat their numbers loosely.
- **TGB on Nov 18.** It fell 9.7% from $6.21 to a low of $5.49, which is today's 20-day low.
  - That session's volume was light (about 1.7M shares against a 5.6M average).
  - About 6,671 puts traded, roughly 182% above average.
  - Freeport was down about 7% and Southern Copper was among the hardest hit.
  - Eleven large copper miners lost about $49B in market value by early afternoon.
- **Earnings on Nov 4-5.** EPS was $0.148 against an estimate of about $0.179. The TSX shares fell about 7% on the release, and the stock was already weak that week. I found no explanation beyond the EPS miss.

**Fundamentals (from the company's Q3 MD&A dated Nov 4, 2026; C$ unless noted)**
- **Results.** Revenue was $342M, up about 97% year over year. Net income was $33.6M, and adjusted EBITDA was a record $164.2M. The realized copper price was US$6.40/lb, so today's copper is about 12% below the Q3 realized price. Operating cash flow was $122M.
- **Gibraltar** (the cash engine; Taseko owns 87.5%). Q3 copper was 33.9M lb, its best quarter this year. C1 cost was US$2.72/lb. 2026 guidance was raised to 115-120M lb from 110-115M lb.
  - One summary says Q4 will be lower on oxidized ore, which I could only see in secondary sources.
  - Diesel and explosives add about US$0.20-0.30/lb.
- **Florence Copper** (in-situ copper recovery in Arizona, ramping up). Q3 output was 7.0M lb, up about 35% from Q2, and C1 cost fell to US$3.54 from US$4.72.
  - 141 wells were producing, 32 came online in the quarter, and six rigs are on site.
  - The wellfield is about three months behind plan, and full 85M lb/yr capacity is now expected in early 2027.
  - 2026 guidance is 25-28M lb. In May it was 30-35M lb, so this looks like a cut. I read both figures in separate sources (the Q3 MD&A and a Q1 call summary), not in a side-by-side comparison. This is the main negative in the fundamentals.
  - The 2027 sulfuric acid contract is still being negotiated, with higher prices expected.
- **Balance sheet.** Cash was $214M and liquidity about $370M. The revolver was extended to October 2029 and enlarged to US$130M. Senior secured notes carry $700M and net debt is $541M. There are also a Florence royalty ($124M) and a copper stream ($113M). One transcript summary says net debt to EBITDA is about 1x.
- **Hedging.** The old collars (US$5.40 cap) cost $41.7M realized in the first nine months, plus $12M settled in Q3. Floor protection now consists of puts on 27M lb at US$4.75 for Q4 and on 45M lb at US$5.00 for H1 2027. That floor limits the downside to the company's cash flow, not to the stock.
- **Yellowhead** (a large development project). The BC environmental assessment was cleared to proceed on July 30, 2026, and it is on the province's priority list.
  - The July 2025 technical report gives an after-tax NPV of C$2.0B, 21% IRR and C$2.0B initial capex, assuming US$4.25/lb copper.
  - It is a long-dated option on copper and not a near-term catalyst.
- **Corporate.** Taseko changed its name to Trekor Metals Limited in June 2026. The tickers are unchanged (TGB, TKO).
- **Analysts.** The MarketBeat consensus is Moderate Buy with an average target of about $9.00 (five Buy, one Hold). Jefferies initiated at Buy in August. I found no downgrade in November.
- **Market data.** Market cap is about $2.0B and beta about 1.44. The stock is below its 50-day ($8.03) and 200-day ($7.61) averages. The 52-week low of $4.14 was set around the October 2025 equity raise at $4.05.

**What this means for a 1-10 session trade**
- **For a bounce:** the move is a copper and positioning flush, not a broken thesis. The company is posting record earnings, the hedge floor is in place, and the RSI-28 reading fits an oversold bounce. Physical tightness could drive a short-covering rally in copper.
- **Against:** copper has not stabilized, and the sentiment drivers (rate hikes, AI unwind, tariff fade) are not resolved. Put buying suggests continued bearish positioning. Florence's guidance cut and its execution risk still weigh on the stock. High leverage amplifies copper moves, and beta is about 1.44.
- **What to watch today:** whether copper holds the Nov 18 low, and whether TGB holds $5.49, which is the 20-day low. The Fed and dollar path matters most. The next scheduled company events I found are Q4 results around February and Florence well-count updates.

**Gaps**
- I couldn't open Benzinga, Daily Political or mining.com (403 errors), so I used search summaries for those.
- I found no copper news dated Nov 19, so today's copper direction is unknown.
- I did not locate the Q3 press release itself, only the MD&A filing with the SEC.

# Annaly (NLY): research as of 9:00 AM CT, Thursday 2026-11-19

I found no company-specific news today and no Annaly news from the past few days. The selloff looks sector-wide and driven by rates. Several sources conflict on figures, which I flag below.

## The story
Annaly is a large mortgage REIT. It holds about $106.5B of assets, funded with about $85.5B of short-term repo borrowing. Its capital is split about 55% Agency MBS (government-backed mortgage bonds), 23% residential credit and 22% mortgage servicing rights (MSR).

The stock is falling because book value is falling. Rates are rising, mortgage spreads are widening, and the Fed is hiking.

**Q3 2026 (reported Oct 20)**
- Book value per share fell 11.4% to $17.86, from $20.15 at June 30. Economic return was -7.6%.
- GAAP net loss was $1.36 per share, which came from unrealized bond losses.
- Earnings available for distribution (EAD) were $0.80 per share against the $0.75 dividend. That beat the $0.77 consensus.
- The 10-year Treasury yield rose 82 bps in the quarter. Agency MBS spreads widened 15-25 bps. September implied volatility hit an 18-month high.
- Leverage rose to 5.9x economic and 8.0x GAAP, mostly because equity shrank.
- The hedge ratio rose to 100% from 97%.
- Net interest spread fell to 1.42% from 1.50%.
- Prepayment speeds slowed (CPR 9.6, down from 11.6), which is a mild positive.

**Capital raising**
- Annaly raised $757M through its at-the-market (ATM) stock program in Q3.
- Shares outstanding rose to 784.7M from 750.6M.
- It redeemed $443M of Series I preferred stock on Oct 1.
- Management calls the ATM sales accretive because the stock traded above book most of the quarter. The sale price isn't disclosed. At today's price, any new issuance would be below Q3 book.

**Sensitivity (from the slides, per Investing.com)**
- A 25 bp widening in MBS spreads cuts net asset value by 10.1%.
- A 50 bp parallel rate rise cuts it by 3.7%.
- Annaly is net long mortgage basis risk. Management says that is deliberate at current spreads.

**Management on the call**
- It expects to outearn the dividend in Q4 and is "comfortable" with the $0.75 quarterly payout.
- Priority order for capital is residential credit, then Agency, then MSR.
- It cited bank capital rule reform as a possible Agency MBS catalyst.
- Book value was up about 2% in the days before the call (about 3% with the dividend accrual). Per management, it was roughly flat since.

## Macro backdrop
- The Fed held at 3.75%-4% on Oct 27-28 in a 10-2 vote. The minutes say further hikes are likely appropriate.
- Waller said Wednesday that a 50 bp hike is "probably necessary" at the Dec 8-9 meeting. He said inflation is persistent and spreading, and "you might need to, like, shock people."
- CME FedWatch prices a 95% chance of a 25 bp hike in December.
- The 10-year yield was about 5.06% on Wednesday, down about 4 bps, and the 30-year was 5.41%. The 2-year was 4.80%.
- Mortgage rate sources disagree. Freddie Mac's Nov 12 survey was 7.11%. Other sources show 7.2-7.4%.
- Management said volatility had eased since September.
- Tikr (Nov 9-10) cited markets pricing close to three more hikes through the end of next year.

## Valuation
- Price-to-book at $16.78 is about 0.94x on the Q3 book of $17.86.
- Book value was reportedly up 2-3% by about Oct 17. That would put it around $18.2 then. I don't have a figure after that, and the rate and spread moves since then are unknown to me.
- If book value has dropped below $17.86, the discount is smaller than it looks.
- The dividend yield is about 17.8% on $3.00 per share.
- Consensus is "Moderate Buy" with an average target of about $21.67 per MarketBeat (a Tikr article says $21). The 12 ratings are 1 Strong Buy, 7 Buy, 3 Hold and 1 Sell.
- After Q3, targets were cut: Barclays $21 (equal weight), RBC $21 (outperform), Wells Fargo $22 (overweight), BofA $19.50 (neutral), JPMorgan about $19-19.50 (overweight), JonesTrading $21 (buy), Piper Sandler $21.50 (overweight, Oct 9). I found no post-Q3 rating downgrades.
- Targets lag price. The stock is now well under all of them.

## Insider and sector signals
- Director Scott Wede bought 50,000 shares on Nov 6 at about $18.80 (about $940K, through his IRA). This is from a Tikr article citing a Form 4, and I could not open the filing itself. The price is now about 11% below his purchase.
- Peers are weak. AGNC closed near $7.89, down about 9.6% in a week and at its lowest since late 2023. Its tangible book value fell 16.9% in Q3 and its leverage is 7.9x.
- AGNC is only about 10.8% above its Q3 tangible book, with a dividend that nearly equals its EAD. That tells you the whole sector is under pressure.

## Price action
- The 52-week low was $17.76 in early to mid October. It broke to about $17.55 around Nov 12, after a 4.2% drop that day to $17.57. NLY hit $16.72 on Nov 18 and is sitting there now.
- NLY traded $18.95 on Nov 9, so it has fallen about 11% in eight sessions.
- MarketBeat shows the 50-day average at $19.18 and the 200-day at $21.62 (the screen has $18.76 and $20.41, so the sources use different dates).
- Volume was about 1.05M shares on Wednesday at the time of that report.

## Risks and flags for the trade (1-10 sessions)
- **Next catalyst:** The Dec 8-9 FOMC is outside or at the edge of the window. Between now and then, the risk is data (CPI, Fed speakers) pushing hike expectations up and spreads wider. Spreads matter more than rate level here, as 25 bp wider means about -10% to net asset value.
- **No fundamental catalyst:** Next earnings are 2027-01-27, so there are no company events in the window.
- **Bounce case:** Volatility has eased since September. Yields fell for three straight sessions into Wednesday. The stock is at a discount to book, and one insider bought. A yield-driven bounce is plausible if spreads stabilize.
- **Falling-knife case:** Waller's 50 bp talk is a clear hawkish shift. The stock is at a new low with no reversal yet, and both moving averages are falling. 24/7 Wall St has run "dividend cut risk" pieces (Nov 12, Nov 18) on mortgage REITs. The ATM issuance also dilutes below book if it continues.
- **Dividend:** Annaly has cut its dividend several times since 2012, including a 26% cut in 2023. Q3 EAD covered it by $0.05. MarketBeat's 210% payout ratio uses GAAP earnings and is not meaningful here.

## Conflicts and gaps
- **Sources disagree on:** the 10-year yield (5.06-5.15%), mortgage rates, the JPMorgan target ($19 vs $19.50), the consensus target ($21 to $23), year-end 2025 book value ($19.25 vs $20.21), and the quoted price-to-book of 0.95 versus 1.02 from one article. I used company filings where possible.
- **Not found:** NLY's book value after mid-October, today's pre-market news, and why the stock fell on Nov 17-18 specifically. MarketBeat's "down 1%" on Nov 18 also doesn't match its own prices ($17.027 vs a $17.04 close).
- **Search status:** After about 15 searches and pages, new searches mostly repeated the same Q3 facts and Fool/MarketBeat commentary.

agents.report:
**FCX research brief, 2026-11-19, about 9:00 AM CT**

**Bottom line.** FCX's drop is mostly a copper and macro event layered on a Grasberg recovery story that was already priced cautiously. Nothing I found points to a new company-specific problem. Copper fell 5-6% on Nov 18, and Erste's downgrade added to that. Copper is bouncing slightly today. I could not confirm today's copper level from a timestamped live source. Whether the stock turns depends on copper stabilizing and on the Fed and dollar. The Grasberg ramp is a slow grind, not a near-term catalyst.

**What happened Nov 18**
- FCX closed at $51.45, down about 7% from $55.30. Its intraday low was $50.46, which matches the screen's 20-day low. [MLQ](https://mlq.ai/news/london-copper-heads-for-its-biggest-one-day-drop-in-19-months-and-freeport-mcmoran-falls-7), [Investing.com](https://www.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/why-is-freeportmcmoran-stock-sliding-today-93CH-5036555)
- LME three-month copper fell 5.5-5.7% to about $12,470-12,500 per ton. That was a fifth straight daily loss, the lowest since Apr 7 and the biggest one-day fall since Apr 2025. Comex copper fell 5-6% to about $5.63-5.70 per lb, a seven-month low. [Globe and Mail](https://www.theglobeandmail.com/investing/article-it-seems-like-people-are-throwing-in-the-towel-why-copper-prices-are/)
- A Saxo strategist said speculators were "throwing in the towel" after technical levels broke, with algorithmic funds adding to the selling. He called the cause an inflation scare and higher funding costs. "AI was a trigger, but it's not really the driver."
- The dollar hit a 19-month high after hawkish remarks from Fed Governor Waller. Markets are leaning toward a Fed rate hike in December. XTB reported on Nov 10 that Waller would back a 25 bp hike in December and left open a 50 bp move. I could not confirm the December odds or the 19-month figure independently. [XTB](https://www.xtb.com/int/market-analysis/news-and-research/waller-s-hawkish-fed-remarks-drive-usdidx-rebound-is-a-50-bp-u-s-rate-hike-possible)
- Other drivers cited:
  - A selloff in AI stocks, which raised worries about data-center copper demand.
  - Rising LME inventories.
  - Chinese demand worries.
  - The unwinding of the tariff premium on US copper.
- Goldman reportedly said copper had been trading like an AI stock, so this is a positioning unwind. Mercuria's Snowdon called current consumption "recessionary-like." These come from secondary summaries, since the Mining.com and Bloomberg pages were not readable. [Bloomberg](https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-11-18/copper-prices-industrial-metal-dollar-lme)
- Sector damage:
  - Southern Copper fell 5.2%, Anglo American 8.0% and Teck 7.4% on the day.
  - Eleven large copper miners lost about $186 billion in a month, according to Mining.com via search summary (one source says $141 billion). [Mining.com](https://www.mining.com/copper-price-craters-as-ai-tariff-trades-unwind-and-asia-copper-week-hears-of-recessionary-like-demand/)
- Physical copper is still tight. Chinese warehouse stocks were at their lowest since Jan 2024 in September. China's import premium hit a record $360 per ton on Wednesday. Smelter fees are reportedly at record lows. The bear case is that the tariff and AI premiums are being squeezed out. The bull case is that thin inventories could set up a short-covering squeeze. [Investing.com](https://www.investing.com/news/commodities-news/copper-slides-despite-tight-physical-supply--what-is-driving-the-selloff-93CH-5036671)
- Today's bounce is small. LME was up about 1.3% to $12,636 early in Asia, but Comex was roughly flat. One Kucoin item claiming a further 6.7% drop looks mis-dated. [Business Recorder](https://www.brecorder.com/news/40449742)

**Company story**
- **Grasberg:** The Sept 2025 mud rush killed seven workers. The Grasberg Block Cave ran at about 67% of capacity in Q3, at roughly 141,000 tons per day. Freeport targets 80% by mid-2027 and near-full capacity by end-2027. [Q3 call transcript](https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/10/27/freeport-mcmoran-fcx-q3-2026-earnings-call-transcript/)
  - Grasberg copper is about 700M lb in 2026, rising to about 1.2B lb in 2027.
  - The PB1 South restart is targeted for 2027. The PB1C restart is still under evaluation.
  - Kucing Liar (a new underground development) is somewhat behind schedule, and one drift hit poor ground.
  - Analysts on the call focused on slower drift development and the timing of the PB1 restart.
- **Guidance:** Sales were trimmed again on the Q3 call. [Q3 transcript](https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/10/27/freeport-mcmoran-fcx-q3-2026-earnings-call-transcript/)

| Item | Figure |
|---|---|
| 2026 copper sales | about 3.0B lb (cut about 2%; the earlier April cut went to 3.1B from 3.4B) |
| 2027 copper sales | about 3.7B lb (cut about 2.5%), with gold up over 50% |
| 2028 copper sales | over 4.0B lb |
| Q4 2026 copper vs Q3 | up about 17% |
| Q4 2026 gold vs Q3 | nearly triples (about 60k oz shifted from Q3 to Q4) |

- **Q3 results:** EPS was $0.88 against $0.82 expected. Revenue was $7.55B. Realized copper was $6.54 per lb. Unit cost was $2.07 per lb against a $2.00 estimate. Full-year guidance of $1.90 per lb is kept. [SEC exhibit](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000831259/000083125926000045/a3q2026exhibit991.htm)
- **Cost pressures:**
  - Idle-facility costs were about $240M in Q3 and over $900M year to date. Management says these move into unit costs from 2027.
  - Diesel has more than doubled, adding about $500M of energy cost in 2026.
  - Sulfuric acid more than doubled.
  - US recoveries are trending lower.
- **Capex:** 2027 capex is $5.2B, up $400M. A Bagdad concentrator expansion of about $4.5B has a final investment decision expected in Q4 2026. This competes with shareholder returns.
- **Balance sheet and returns:**
  - Cash was $4.3B, and net debt was $1.8B excluding $3.2B of project debt.
  - Year-to-date returns were about $1B, including $305M of buybacks.
  - The dividend is $0.075 per quarter, a yield of about 0.6%.
  - Operating cash flow guidance for 2026 is $8.5B, assuming $6.50 per lb copper. That assumption is now well above spot at about $5.65.
- **Sensitivity:** About $390M of EBITDA per $0.10 per lb of copper. Modeled 2027-28 EBITDA is over $12B at $5 copper and $19.5B at $7. Copper at $5 is still profitable but far from what the stock was pricing.
- **Indonesia:** The February 2026 MoU extends rights beyond 2041. FCX would hold 48.76% through 2041 and about 37% from 2042. The amended IUPK permit was applied for in June and was still pending as of the latest coverage I found, from August. Issuance would be a positive headline, but I found no timing. [FCX release](https://investors.fcx.com/investors/news-releases/news-release-details/2026/FCX-Announces-Agreement-for-Life-of-Resource-Extension-of-Operating-Rights-in-Grasberg-Minerals-District/default.aspx)
- **Tariffs:** A 50% tariff on semi-finished copper has applied since Aug 2025. The refined-copper decision passed its deadline without action, and the tariff premium has largely deflated. The Comex-LME spread is now narrow, so a surprise tariff announcement is a two-way risk. [ConnectOre](https://connectore.org/posts/copper-weekly-brief-2nd-october-2026/)

**Analysts and ownership**
- Erste cut FCX to Hold from Buy on Nov 18, citing near-term copper and gold output declines as Grasberg ramps up, and valuation. No target was given. [Investing.com](https://www.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/why-is-freeportmcmoran-stock-sliding-today-93CH-5036555)
- Consensus is "Moderate Buy" (1 Strong Buy, 19 Buy, 5 Hold) with an average target of $75.30. After the Oct 28 cuts, JPMorgan is at $90, UBS at $85 and Wells Fargo at $79. Bernstein is at $47 (market perform) as of Sept 9. [MarketBeat](https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/price-freeport-mcmoran-nyse-fcx-shares-gap-down-after-analyst-downgrade-2026-11-18/)
- Morgan Stanley downgraded to Equal Weight in April. [247WallSt](https://247wallst.com/investing/2026/04/24/morgan-stanley-downgrades-freeport-mcmoran-is-the-copper-story-breaking-down-at-grasberg/)
- Valuation per MarketBeat: market cap about $74B, trailing P/E about 21, beta 1.38. That P/E was computed at the pre-drop price.
- Insiders sold near $78-79 in late August: EVP Currault sold 80,000 shares, and a director sold 3,798.
- I found no short-interest data.

**Timeline**
- Aug: stock near $79-80, the 52-week high of about $80.
- Sept-Oct: copper and LME hit records. The Comex-LME spread blew out to about $15,100 per ton on tariff bets, then deflated.
- Oct 27: Q3 beat on earnings, with guidance trimmed.
- Oct 28: price-target cuts.
- Early Nov: copper down five straight sessions, then the Nov 18 break.

**Read for a 1-10 session trade**
- **Bounce case:**
  - The selloff is a sentiment and positioning unwind (RSI 27, 3.1 average daily ranges below the 20-day average).
  - Physical tightness could support copper.
  - Analyst targets sit far above $51.83, and Q4 shipments should rise 17%.
  - The $50.46 low is a nearby technical line.
- **Risks:**
  - The December Fed hike is a live macro risk and could push the dollar higher.
  - Momentum funds may keep selling after the broken technical levels.
  - FCX has moved very closely with COPX, so it will follow any sector move.
  - There is no company catalyst before the Jan 21 report.
  - Erste's downgrade and the earlier guidance cuts show estimate risk.
- **What to watch:**
  - Whether copper holds near $5.60-5.65 and the LME $12,400-12,500 area.
  - The dollar and Fed headlines.
  - A refined-copper tariff headline.
  - Any Grasberg or Indonesian permit news.
  - The Bagdad final investment decision in Q4.

**Gaps.** I found no news dated Nov 19 specific to FCX. I could not confirm a Grasberg status update after Q3, the Manyar smelter restart, or short interest. Several pages blocked fetching, so some copper details come from search summaries.

**BNS (Bank of Nova Scotia, NYSE) research, 2026-11-19, about 9:00 AM CT.** I ran 16 searches and opened 10 pages. The last several searches turned up almost nothing new, apart from the gaps listed at the end.

**The story in brief**
BNS is a sound, improving bank that rallied hard and is now pulling back with the Canadian bank group. I found no company-specific bad news. The slide looks like a sector and macro move, which is what the screen's "stretched down, no turn yet" reading would suggest.

**How the stock got here**
- The 52-week range of $64.07 to $96.85 and a one-year return of about 45% fit a big re-rating. One source puts the Toronto price at about C$131 on 11/12.
- BNS set a 52-week high of $96.17 on 10/29, per Weiss. On 11/5 it fell 4.5% to $92.05 (from $96.43), which Weiss attributed to a broad US selloff on midterm-election fears. Weiss said the selloff also hit other financials and Canadian banks, and cited no BNS-specific news.
- On 11/16 and 11/17 the Toronto market fell, led by banks.
  - On 11/17, TD fell 1.8%, BMO 2%, RBC 1.6%, and the TSX 1.1%. Tradingeconomics did not mention Scotiabank.
  - BNS fell 1.7% to C$127.47 midday on 11/17 on light volume, about 1.3M shares against a 4.1M average.
- Reported drivers of the Canadian bank selloff:
  - **Oil and inflation:** oil rebounded on continued Middle East shipping attacks (the US-Iran conflict), which revives inflation fears.
  - **Bank of Canada:** it raised its rate 25 basis points to 2.5% on 10/28, the first hike in three years. The 11/10 summary of deliberations said further hikes might be needed. The next decision is 12/9.
  - **Tech selloff:** a global tech selloff over Nvidia's role as a financial backstop for AI companies. This is risk-off pressure, not a bank issue.
- Valuation is stretched, from secondary sources. BNN Bloomberg's Thackray (8/28) said the sector trades at a trailing P/E of about 17.4 against a 20-year average near 11.8, "priced for perfection". A Fundmore.ai blog says forward valuations are the highest since 2010. Treat that blog cautiously.
- MarketBeat's 11/17 snapshot gives BNS a P/E of 16.7 and a 50-day average of C$130.10 against a 200-day of C$116.05. That is the same uptrend structure your screen shows.

**Fundamentals (Q3 FY26, reported 8/25)**
- Reported net income was $2,953M and adjusted was $2,973M, a record quarter. Adjusted EPS was $2.28 against $1.88 a year earlier. Adjusted return on equity was 14.2%, above the 14% target, and management said 14% is not a ceiling.
- Segment earnings, year over year:

| Segment | Earnings | Change |
|---|---|---|
| Canadian Banking | $1,071M | +12% |
| International Banking | $725M | +8% |
| Global Wealth Management | $515M | +23% |
| Global Banking and Markets | $647M | +37% (record) |

- Provisions for credit losses were $1.08B, 56 basis points of loans, down 10 basis points from the prior quarter. International Banking provisions were 138 basis points, with a single Brazil account needing an extra $57M. Management flagged elevated mortgage delinquencies as a watch item.
- Capital: the common equity tier 1 ratio was 13.1%, down 20 basis points. The bank bought back 8.6M shares and says it favors buybacks given a valuation gap.
- Q4 items management flagged:
  - Moving certain International portfolios to the advanced internal ratings approach costs about 15 basis points of capital, so it expects CET1 near 13%.
  - A one-time deferred tax asset write-down from Chile's tax cut.
  - Impaired provisions trending down in the second half.
  - "Finish the year strong."
- The strategy is a turnaround under CEO Scott Thomson. The bank has exited Colombia, Costa Rica and Panama and is refocusing on North America, with Mexico, Chile and the Caribbean kept. The Fool.ca author calls it "turnaround mode". The bank says the tariff effect is small, with affected loans under 1% of total loans. Trade tensions remain a risk, since one source says the Canada-US trade deal recently broke down.

**Analysts (MarketBeat 11/17)**
- Consensus is Moderate Buy: 1 strong buy, 4 buy, 7 hold. The average target is about C$129.89, close to the current price, so little upside is implied.
- Raymond James raised its target to C$142.50 (Outperform, 11/17).

**For the 1-10 session decision**

agents.report:
**Refiners (MPC, VLO, PSX, PBF, DINO, DK, CVI, PARR): story as of Thursday 2026-11-19, about 9:00 AM CT**

**Bottom line:** The group is falling on fear that record margins have peaked, not on any company news. Earnings are at records, but the market is pricing a unwind. I found no new catalyst for today. The weak spots are the gasoline crack, a crude build, and Washington headline risk. The support is diesel margins that are still very high, deep valuation discounts, and heavy buybacks and dividends. My read is neutral to mildly bearish for 1-3 sessions, with a snap-back possible over 5-10 sessions. The next EIA report is Nov 25, a Wednesday, and nothing scheduled falls in between.

**1. What happened to prices**
- Valero hit a 52-week high of $459.78 on Oct 14. It is down 20.7% over the past month and still up about 114% year to date (Trefis).
- Oct 27 was the worst day for refiners since the April 2025 tariff shock. VLO fell 9.2% to $387.34, MPC 7.4% and PSX 7.0%, about $29B of market value in one session. Fuel futures fell faster than crude (heating oil -2.8%, RBOB -2.5%, WTI -1.8%). Trump posted that gasoline and diesel prices would "soon come plummeting down." VLO had already opened below its prior close, so no single headline explains it ([Yahoo/Benzinga](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/refiner-stocks-just-had-worst-193947356.html)).
- Nov 4 was the day after Marathon's strong Q3. MPC fell about 10%, DINO 9%, VLO 8% and PSX 6%. TIKR links it to Democrats winning the Senate in the midterms. That is a single source and uncertain ([TIKR](https://www.tikr.com/blog/marathon-petroleum-sinks-10-valero-down-8-as-oil-stocks-slide-after-democrats-win-the-senate)).
- Nov 13 to 16: Mizuho cut its MPC target from $457 to $440 and kept a neutral rating. MPC fell 3.1% ([MarketBeat](https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/price-marathon-petroleum-nyse-mpc-shares-down-31-after-analyst-downgrade-2026-11-16/)). The sources disagree on the day of the note.
- Nov 18 was another broad drop with no company news. VLO fell 5.5%, MPC 5.2%, PSX 4.7%, and XLE 3.3%. Six of seven peers fell more than 5%. Par Pacific fell 6.5%, and PBF, DK and CVI fell about 5-6% ([Trefis](https://www.trefis.com/stock/vlo/articles/626950/what-sent-valero-energy-stock-lower/2026-11-19)). Coverage called it sector contagion. Trefis said the cause was likely the shared crack-spread business and named no trigger.
- Our screen reads down 14.8% against XLE over 20 sessions, with all eight below their 50-day averages. That is consistent with the above.

**2. Margins: falling, but unevenly**
- The 3-2-1 crack was about $41.8 on Nov 17. That is roughly $33 below the October peak of about $75. The September monthly average was $68.23, the highest since 2006 ([Global Biodiesel Substack](https://globalbiodiesel.substack.com/p/post-election-321-crack-slide-tests), [GlobalOilShock](https://globaloilshock.com/en/data/crack-spread-chart/)). Sources vary from about $37 to $46 by method and contract month.
- Gasoline caused most of the drop, and the gasoline crack is now below $20. The December diesel crack was about $84-86, level with WTI. The Substack author treats $85 as a key level and says a settle below it would end his long-distillate view.
- Bearish supply factors:
  - The IEA sees a Q4 surplus above 1.7 mb/d.
  - A 15 million barrel diesel stock release is planned through February.
  - Gulf loadings rebounded to 10.4 mb/d.
  - Tanker rates halved over two weeks.
- The Nov 18 EIA report (week ended Nov 13) showed crude up 3.4 million barrels, gasoline up 5.2 million, and distillates up 1.6 million. Refinery utilization was 95.7% ([BOE Report/Reuters](https://boereport.com/2026/11/18/us-crude-stocks-gasoline-and-distillate-inventories-rise-eia-says/)). Product builds at that utilization are bearish for cracks.
- Brent is about $92 and WTI about $82-83 today. Reports of Hormuz mines and tanker attacks lifted prices slightly, but a surplus outlook caps them ([Anadolu](https://www.aa.com.tr/en/energy/oil/oil-prices-rise-on-hormuz-shipping-risks-as-surplus-outlook-caps-gains/61115)).
- The Substack source says Hormuz has been effectively closed for 262 days. A separate report says Gulf exports are near pre-war levels. These conflict.
- The US Strategic Petroleum Reserve is at 276.4 million barrels, its lowest since 1982.

**3. Fundamentals are at records**
- **VLO (Oct 22):** Adjusted EPS $23.90 against a $20.30 consensus. Refining margin was $39.24 per barrel, up from $13.14. Management said margins are "very sustainable" and warned a crude run-up could squeeze them. It is buying LyondellBasell's former Houston refinery for $320.5M. It trades at 0.64x sales.
- **MPC (Nov 3):** Adjusted EPS $26.93, about 40% of full-year consensus. RIN spend was $654M. It was at about 5.3x forward earnings before the Nov 4 drop, roughly the 2022 low. It is selling its St. Paul Park and Mandan refineries to CVR.
- **DINO:** Adjusted EPS $11.75 and refinery margin $54.22 per barrel, helped by small refinery exemptions. It returned $572M to holders, paid a $0.525 dividend, and is preparing a lubricants separation ([HF Sinclair](https://investor.hfsinclair.com/investor-relations/press-releases/press-releases-details/2026/HF-Sinclair-Reports-2026-Third-Quarter-Results-and-Announces-Regular-Cash-Dividend/default.aspx)). It was at about 4.9x forward earnings before the drop.
- **PBF (Oct 29):** EPS $12.54. It cut net debt by more than $1.2B and raised its dividend 18% to $0.325 ([Morningstar](https://www.morningstar.com/news/pr-newswire/20261029ny84280/pbf-energy-announces-third-quarter-2026-results-declares-dividend-of-0325-per-share)).
- **PARR:** GAAP EPS $7.11, or $10.70 adjusted including a $222M small-refinery-exemption benefit. It reached net cash for the first time ever, with $731M of cash ([GuruFocus](https://www.gurufocus.com/news/9169081/par-pacific-holdings-reports-q3-2026-earnings-eps-of-711-and-revenue-of-305-billion-exceed-analyst-estimates)).
- **CVI:** EPS $5.67 and adjusted EPS $4.00. The Group 3 2-1-1 crack averaged $68.50. It is buying the two Marathon refineries for about $4.2B, with closing expected by year-end ([call summary](https://www.tradingkey.com/news/transcripts/262269823-)). Pro forma debt would be about $3.8B. Management expects elevated margins for 12-24 months. RIN costs were $235M in the quarter.
- **DK:** It had the biggest Q3 EPS beat among energy names, at $5.43 per Seeking Alpha. Net debt is $2.05B. I could not get more detail.
- **PSX:** Refining was about four-fifths of segment pre-tax earnings.
- Analysts expect 2028 earnings at about half of 2026 levels (TIKR). Jefferies downgraded VLO and MPC to Hold on Sept 22 ([Seeking Alpha](https://seekingalpha.com/news/4645636-valero-marathon-cut-at-jefferies-supporting-less-refining-exposure-after-big-gains)). The MPC consensus target is about $424.

**4. Policy and headline risks**
- **Windfall tax:** The Whitehouse/Khanna bill would tax profits when Brent is above about $68. Rapidan puts the chance of a windfall tax or cut to fossil-fuel tax breaks at 30%. ClearView thinks a deal with Trump is unlikely. Democrats take Congress in January 2027, so this is a slow-burn overhang with no vote soon ([Rigzone](https://www.rigzone.com/news/wire/oil_sector_girds_for_possible_windfall_tax-05-nov-2026-185018-article/)).
- **Diesel export ban:** Thune said in September he was "open to exploring" one. Citigroup's Bagri warned a full ban would end the margin and share-price run. Energy Secretary Wright and Interior Secretary Burgum oppose it. No ban is in force, and I could not find a current status ([OPIS](https://www.opis.com/resources/energy-market-news-from-opis/senate-majority-leader-thune-open-to-exploring-diesel-export-ban/)).
- **Russian diesel deal:** Trump announced it Oct 9 and Treasury issued General License 135 through April 7, 2027. It conflicts with a 2022 import ban, and no cargoes have landed. Tankers turned around ([Lawfare](https://www.lawfaremedia.org/article/dissecting-trump-s-deal-for-russian-diesel), [RedState](https://redstate.com/streiff/2026/11/13/trump-putin-diesel-deal-flops-tankers-u-turn-as-legal-risks-scare-off-buyers-n2209376)). The diesel imports are therefore a small real supply, but they still drive headlines.
- **RINs and small refinery exemptions:** RINs are above $14/bbl and are a cost for the non-integrated names. Exemptions boosted DINO's and PARR's Q3 results, and the Tikr piece notes EPA rule risk.
- **Other:** The Substack lists a US-China-Russia summit in Shenzhen on Thursday and any US-Iran diplomacy as swing factors. Better US-Iran relations hurt refiners, because the Oct 27 selloff was tied to the possibility of the war ending.

**5. Reading for the trade**
- **Why a bounce is plausible:**
  - The group is at extreme oversold levels against XLE, with all eight below their 50-day averages.
  - Valuations are around 5x earnings.
  - Q3 cash returns are large.
  - Diesel cracks are still elevated.
  - There have been multiple big drops without new fundamental news.
- **Why it may not turn yet:**
  - There is no turn so far. The group is still down 0.5% this morning.
  - Gasoline cracks and product inventories are still heading the wrong way.
  - The market is pricing 2028 earnings at half of 2026 levels, so the "cheap" multiples are on peak earnings.
  - A dip below an $85 diesel crack, or a crude-led squeeze, would add pressure.
  - Political headline risk is skewed to the downside.
- **Within the group:**
  - CVI and PARR carry deal or balance-sheet stories (the Marathon refineries purchase and the net cash position).
  - PBF, DK and PARR are the high-beta names. They moved most on Nov 18.
  - MPC, VLO and PSX are the large caps, but VLO and MPC are still up 114% and 190% year to date, so there is more to unwind.
  - DINO and MPC are both on the Mizuho and TIKR radar.

**Gaps:** I could not open the Benzinga or Chartmill pages (403) or the AlphaStreet page. I have no verified share prices for today, and no Delek-specific call details. Several figures come from aggregator sites rather than company filings. I found no explanation for the Nov 18 drop beyond the crude and product builds. The "Democrats won the Senate" link for Nov 4 rests on one source.

Sources used: links inline above, plus [FinanceFeeds](https://financefeeds.com/brent-crude-oil-price-92-12-thursday-eia-build-hormuz-mines-bull-96-bear-88/), [Benzinga on the Trump-Putin deal](https://www.benzinga.com/markets/commodities/26/10/62499797/trump-putin-diesel-deal-refiner-stocks-valero-pbf-marathon), and [Seeking Alpha on Q3 EPS beats](https://seekingalpha.com/news/4672890-as-q3-earnings-season-nears-end-these-10-energy-stocks-stand-out-for-eps-beats).
