**Freeport-McMoRan (FCX) research, as of 9:25 AM CT on Thursday 2026-11-19.** The drop is a copper-wide macro selloff. Company-specific news is mild, and no source says anything has broken at Freeport itself.

**Why it is stretched down**
- **The drop:** FCX fell 6.96% on Nov 18 to $51.45, after being $55.30 the previous close and about $55.19 on Nov 16. Its intraday low was $50.46, which is the screen's 20-day low.
- **Copper's worst day in over a year:** Three-month LME copper fell 3.5% to $12,770 a tonne, the lowest since April and the fifth straight daily decline. COMEX copper fell about 5% to roughly $5.66 a pound, a seven-month low. One report puts COMEX near $5.58 on Nov 19, but I could not confirm that.
- **About 20% below the September peak:** The LME record was above $14,700 in early September, and COMEX peaked near $6.80. Copper was on track for its longest run of weekly declines in two years.
- **Macro drivers, with no single cause confirmed:**
  - The dollar is near a 19-month high.
  - Hawkish Fed minutes released Nov 18 showed almost all officials saw further rate rises as likely appropriate. Futures price roughly even odds of a hike.
  - Weak October China data.
  - Doubts about AI data-center spending.
  - Technical selling after key support broke.
  - Saxo's Ole Hansen blamed the inflation scare and funding costs more than AI, saying AI "was a trigger, but it's not really the driver".
- **Tariff premium narrowing:** Doubts that refined-copper tariffs will go ahead after the midterms narrowed the New York premium over London.
- **Peers fell too:** On Nov 18, Southern Copper fell 5.9%, Teck 6.5% and COPX 5.4% to 6.3%, depending on the source. This fits the screen's close tracking of COPX.
- **Erste downgrade:** On Nov 18, Erste Group cut FCX to Hold from Buy on expected production declines and valuation (P/E about 23). The stock opened at $52.18 after the downgrade.

**Fundamentals**
- **Q3 2026 results (Oct 2026):** Adjusted EPS was $0.88 against $0.80 expected, and revenue $7.55B against $7.36B expected. The realized copper price was above $6.50 a pound. Unit net cash cost was $2.07 a pound, with $1.90 guided for the full year.
- **Grasberg recovery from the mud rush:** Mill throughput was about 67% of normal. The company guides to 80% of capacity by mid-2027 and near full capacity by the end of 2027. Production Block 1 South restarts by mid-2027, and the PB1C restart is deferred to late 2027, with a minor contribution in 2028.
- **Guidance trimmed:** 2026 copper sales are about 3.0B lb, trimmed about 2%. 2027 is 3.7B lb, up more than 20%, trimmed about 2.5%, and gold is up more than 50%. 2028 production is over 4B lb.
- **Cost and capex pressure:** Diesel adds about $500M versus 2025, and sulfuric acid prices more than doubled. Capex is about $4.4B in 2026 and $5.2B in 2027. Idle Grasberg costs of about $240M in Q3 move into unit costs from 2027.
- **US operations:** Q3 rates were below plan because of flooding, power outages and wind. Recoveries have trended lower, and Arizona labor is tight.
- **Sensitivity to price:** Each $0.10 a pound change in copper moves annual EBITDA by about $390M. Operating cash flow is over $9B a year at $5 copper and about $15B at $7.
- **Capital return and balance sheet:** Nearly $1B returned year to date, including $300M of buybacks. PT Freeport Indonesia priced $750M of 6.90% notes due 2033 to refinance debt. Indonesia's contract has been extended to 2061.
- **Analysts:** The MarketBeat consensus is Moderate Buy with an average target of about $75.30. Late-October cuts were JPMorgan $92 to $90, UBS $88 to $85, Wells Fargo $87 to $79 and Scotiabank $80 to $78. Freedom Broker cut to $68 with a Hold, dated either Oct 28 or Nov 2.

**Today's setup**
- A Nov 19 morning brief shows premarket FCX up 1.87%, Southern Copper up 1.91% and Teck up 2.78%. SPY is up 1.27% and QQQ up 2.19%.
- A Nov 19 AI-sector bounce is helping: Nvidia is rising and Palo Alto jumped.
- The screen shows FCX up only 0.7% by 8:50 AM CT, so the premarket gain has faded.
- The Wednesday low of $50.46 is the line to watch.
- No FCX-specific catalyst is scheduled before the 2027-01-21 earnings report.

**What I could not confirm**
- Any Nov 2026 Grasberg or Indonesian export news.
- Tariff policy details.
- Positioning data.
- The exact Nov 19 copper price.

**Read for a 1-10 session trade**
- **Bull case:** Physical demand looks strong. China's import premium hit a record $360 a tonne on Nov 18, and Glencore cut 2026 output guidance to 810,000-870,000 tonnes, but LME stocks of about 320,000 tonnes are near six-year highs. Oversold readings and Grasberg volume growth into 2027 also support a bounce.
- **Bear case:** The move is macro-led, so the Fed, the dollar and Chinese data decide direction. The Hold downgrade and tariff-premium erosion add to it, and a break below $50.46 could extend the slide.
- **Where this leaves a trade:** It is a rebound-or-breakdown bet on copper and risk sentiment, not on FCX itself.

**KTOS research brief as of 9:20 AM CT, Thu 2026-11-19**

The decline looks like a valuation and sector de-rating, not a broken business. I found no stock-specific bad news. The bounce today has no catalyst I could find.

**Setup**
- Kratos makes Valkyrie jet drones, hypersonic test vehicles and rocket systems, turbojet engines, microwave electronics, and satellite ground systems.
- The stock peaked around $134 on Jan 16, at about 183 times forward earnings ([TIKR](https://www.tikr.com/blog/kratos-sinks-15-in-a-week-to-a-new-52-week-low-is-the-selling-overdone)). It is now about $30, down roughly 60% year to date ([24/7 Wall St.](https://247wallst.com/investing/2026/11/18/aerovironment-is-near-its-52-week-low-will-avav-stock-hit-50-or-150-first)).
- The decline started well before Q3. The stock traded around $72 in late March, $61 in April, and $45 at the July 52-week low ([MarketBeat](https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/kratos-defense-security-solutions-nasdaqktos-hits-new-52-week-low-time-to-sell-2026-07-29/)).
- In March the company sold 14.29M shares at $84, about $1.2B gross, to fund drone and hypersonic plants. A B. Riley valuation downgrade landed around the same time ([Rallies](https://rallies.ai/news/kratos-slides-as-valuation-downgrade-hits-amid-lingering-117b-share-sale-overhang)).

**Q3 report (Nov 5) and the October-November slide**
- Q3 revenue was $471.8M, up 35.7% (23.2% organic), in line with estimates. Adjusted EPS was $0.24 against $0.21 expected ([StockStory](https://stockstory.org/us/stocks/nasdaq/ktos/news/earnings-call/ktos-q3-2026-deep-dive-management-highlights-drone-production-ramp-and-supply-chain-risks)).
- Bookings were $1.04B (2.2 book-to-bill). Backlog was a record of about $2.6-2.65B (sources vary slightly). Adjusted EBITDA was $50.9M, above the $40-45M guide.
- FY26 guidance is revenue of $1.78-1.81B and adjusted EBITDA of $176-180M. The initial 2027 guide is revenue of $2.1-2.2B and adjusted EBITDA of $230-240M, slightly below the roughly $2.23B consensus ([Motley Fool transcript](https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/11/06/kratos-defense-ktos-q3-2026-earnings-call-transcript/)).
- Management said its internal 2027 forecast is "considerably higher" than the published one. The guide assumes the continuing resolution is resolved by March 31, 2027. If it runs longer, management said it would reassess.
- Management expects about $700M of hypersonics revenue in 2027. It plans to roughly triple Firejet drone capacity by the end of 2027.
- The weak spots are cash and margin:
  - Q3 free cash flow was negative $29.4M.
  - Receivables days outstanding rose to 125 from 114.
  - Operating margin was about -1%.
  - Management targets positive cash flow only by 2029.
  - The turbojet program alone needs about $130-140M of working capital through mid-2027.
  - The CEO said the company is "totally capitalized" with no raise expected.
  - The call did not cover Valkyrie production detail beyond a restricted-customer low-rate initial production contract. The CEO said the Air Force CCA Increment 1 awards went to Anduril and General Atomics.
- The stock was roughly flat after hours on the report. It then fell 15% over the week to a 52-week low on Nov 6-7, mostly tracking a growth and AI-hardware selloff with no company news ([TIKR](https://www.tikr.com/blog/kratos-sinks-15-in-a-week-to-a-new-52-week-low-is-the-selling-overdone)).
- The CFO sold 266,740 shares at $40 on Oct 29 ([Fox Business](https://www.foxbusiness.com/quote?stockTicker=KTOS)). Director Steven Fendley sold 14,000 shares at $33.85 on Nov 13, and the stock fell 6.6% to $31.66 on Nov 16 on 4.0M shares, about average volume ([MarketBeat](https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/price-kratos-defense-security-solutions-nasdaq-ktos-stock-falls-66-on-insider-selling-2026-11-16/)).
- The stock closed at $31.06 on Nov 17 and fell 2.6% on Nov 18 ([MarketBeat](https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/price-kratos-defense-security-solutions-nasdaq-ktos-stock-falls-26-heres-what-happened-2026-11-18/)). That is consistent with your $31.17 being up 3.1% today.

**Sector and macro**
- The whole group is down. AeroVironment is down about 58% year to date and Red Cat about 72%. Drivers cited are 30-year yields near 19-year highs, a New York Fed official hinting at rate hikes, budget-timing uncertainty, and funding delays at smaller names ([24/7 Wall St.](https://247wallst.com/investing/2026/11/18/aerovironment-is-near-its-52-week-low-will-avav-stock-hit-50-or-150-first), [Aug 20 piece](https://247wallst.com/investing/2026/08/20/ondas-drops-7-unusual-machines-sinks-8-kratos-falls-5-as-the-drone-trade-unwinds/)).
- One search summary mentioned a 52-week low after Democrats won both chambers of Congress. I could not confirm this and its date is unclear, so treat it as unverified.
- The same summary said a Kratos space program was canceled with $1.5B of backlog wiped out. That is wrong. The article it came from was about AeroVironment's BADGER SCAR program, and I found no Kratos cancellation.

**Valuation and sentiment**
- Forward P/E was about 34 at the early-November price, against a five-year average of 58 (TIKR). Trailing P/E is over 250, and net margin is about 1.3%.
- Market cap is about $6B. Debt-to-equity is 0.05 and the current ratio is 5.4.
- Analyst consensus is "Moderate Buy" (2 Strong Buy, 22 Buy, 1 Hold, 1 Sell) with an average target of $77.40. Targets are still being cut:
  - Barclays cut to $80 on Nov 10.
  - B. Riley cut to $91 on Oct 30.
  - Goldman cut to $77 in October.
  - BTIG cut to $65 from $104.
  - Noble raised its 2027 EPS estimate but cut Q4 2026 to $0.15.
- Short interest is about 5.7% of shares (10.7M shares, 2.7 days to cover), up about 10% from the prior reading. That figure comes from an aggregator ([Equibles](https://equibles.com/stocks/KTOS)).
- Institutions hold about 76%.

**Catalysts and risks over 1-10 sessions**
- **Dates:** The Q4 report is early 2027 (one source says Feb 22), outside the window. I found no scheduled company event inside the window.
- **Positive possibilities:** new contract announcements, a budget or appropriations resolution, and a drone or defense sector bounce.
- **Negative possibilities:**
  - More insider selling.
  - Further rate pressure on high-multiple stocks.
  - A new share sale. TIKR flags the cash burn as a risk, though management denies the need.
  - Sector news such as Red Cat's missed targets spilling over.
- **What I could not find:** any news for Nov 18-19 explaining today's bounce, and a confirmed FINRA short-interest figure.

**Read for the journal**
- This is a mean-reversion bounce from near the 52-week low of $29.98, with the stock about 4% above it.
- The bounce is in the top quarter of the day's range on light volume, which is weak confirmation.
- Both moving averages are falling and the sector trend is down. Insider selling and the cash-burn story are the main stock-specific negatives, and the record backlog and conservative guide are the main positives.
- A close below $29.98 would break the lows. A hold with sector stabilization could retrace toward the $35-37 area, which was the pre-selloff level.
- Overall, the story supports a short-term bounce attempt but not a trend change.

agents.report:
**BioNTech (BNTX) research brief, as of the morning of 2026-11-19**

**Bottom line:** The story has two parts. Cash and a buyback give BioNTech a floor, and the COVID business is shrinking. The valuation turns on whether pumitamig, its PD-L1xVEGF cancer antibody partnered with Bristol Myers Squibb, can show survival benefit. A new negative read-through for that drug class arrived on Nov 15. The drop below the 52-week closing low is probably that read-through, but I found no article tying today's BNTX move to it, so that is my inference.

**What the company is now**
- It is a COVID-vaccine cash machine turning into an oncology company, and the bet rests on pumitamig.
- Q3 2026 (reported Nov 3):
  - Revenue was €1.289B, down from €1.519B a year earlier, on lower COVID vaccine demand.
  - IFRS net profit was €184.5M. Year to date it is still a €1.168B loss.
  - About €613M of Q3 revenue was attributed to the BMS pumitamig partnership (one source's figure).
- 2026 revenue guidance was narrowed up to €1.7–1.9B, from €1.6–1.9B. R&D and SG&A guidance were unchanged.
- Cash and securities are €16.16B, about €65 per share on 247.9M shares. At roughly $82.5 per ADS that is substantial cash support, though I haven't converted currencies.
- Buyback:
  - Up to $1.0B, running to May 6, 2027.
  - Through Sep 30 it bought 5.04M ADSs at an average of $91.98 (about $463M).
  - About $537M of capacity remains.
  - I did not find whether it has been buying since.
- Restructuring:
  - Impairments were €223M in Q3 (€414M year to date).
  - Employee-related restructuring costs were €19.7M in Q3 (€125M year to date).
  - Manufacturing sites in Idar-Oberstein, Marburg, Tübingen and Singapore, plus CureVac sites, are being wound down, affecting up to about 1,860 jobs.
  - A works council letter reported by Handelsblatt criticizes management; these are unverified assertions.
- It opted to shift future R&D costs on a Roche/Genentech program (the pancreatic cancer vaccine, autogene cevumeran) to Roche from Jan 1, 2027. BioNTech keeps royalty eligibility.
- It is buying an FDA priority review voucher from Scholar Rock for $205M cash (announced about Nov 10).
  - Closing is pending antitrust (HSR) clearance.
  - The target drug is unnamed; media guess pumitamig.
  - A voucher cuts the FDA review from 10 months to 6.

**Why the stock is weak**
- Oct 13: BNT113 (head and neck cancer) missed its progression-free survival endpoint in a Phase 2/3 trial. The stock fell about 5–7%. The trial continues toward an overall survival endpoint.
- Q3 report, Nov 3–4:
  - The stock slid about 1–4%, roughly $86–91.
  - Analysts cut targets but mostly kept their ratings. Wells Fargo went to $125 from $140 (Overweight). Morgan Stanley went to $106 from $114, BofA to $108 from $114, and H.C. Wainwright to $110 from $130.
  - BMO downgraded to Market Perform on Sep 8, with a $105 target, citing COVID demand.
  - MarketBeat consensus is "Moderate Buy" at about $123.60.
- Nov 15 (Sunday): the FDA issued a complete response letter (a rejection) to Summit's ivonescimab, a competing PD-1xVEGF drug. Summit shares fell about 13–16% on Monday and about 10% more on Tuesday.
  - The drug was for EGFR-mutant lung cancer. Overall survival was 18.6 vs 14 months, not statistically significant.
  - The FDA said progression-free survival alone does not support approval. Fierce also reports it cited China-heavy data (I could not open that article).
  - Summit has been asked to run a new global trial for that indication.
  - BMO said BioNTech "will need to take note." The class now faces a demand to prove overall survival.
  - Summit's next test is HARMONi-3 in squamous lung cancer, due by year-end. A result that misses or looks weak would likely hit BNTX again, and a clean win would help it.
- Underlying fade: Fierce reported at ASCO that BioNTech/BMS and Pfizer are divided on how to handle overall survival. BioNTech/BMS recently redesigned the first-line NSCLC trial to make progression-free survival the single primary endpoint. After the Summit letter that choice is an exposure; I did not see commentary on it.

**Upcoming catalysts and risks**
- Gotistobart (PRESERVE-003, Phase 3, squamous NSCLC): the first interim analysis of stage 2 is expected in 2026, timing dependent on events. It could be unblinded or continue. Stage 1 data at WCLC showed overall survival nearly doubled vs chemotherapy.
- Pumitamig data so far:
  - 2L NSCLC with docetaxel: 36.7% confirmed response rate, 90% disease control, 30 evaluable patients.
  - Small cell lung cancer: 76.3% response rate, 6.8-month median progression-free survival.
  - Triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC): encouraging Phase 2 data.
  - Phase 3 starts: a TNBC trial with Gilead's sacituzumab govitecan, and small cell lung cancer (overall survival primary endpoint, completion about 2029).
  - No pivotal overall survival readouts are near-term.
- Trastuzumab pamirtecan: BioNTech and DualityBio are discussing a possible BLA. The progression-free survival benefit was modest and the rate of interstitial lung disease (ILD) was higher.
- Legal: Arbutus/Genevant expanded lipid nanoparticle patent suits against Pfizer/BioNTech in Canada and Japan. A Levi & Korsinsky "investigation" notice is a typical plaintiff-firm solicitation.
- COVID: the 2026/27 XFG vaccine launched, but US eligibility is limited to adults 65+ and high-risk people aged 5–64. Demand is structurally declining.
- Next scheduled earnings: Mar 2, 2027, so none falls in the 1–10 session window.

**Read for a 1–10 session trade**
- Bearish: the stock is below a falling 50-day and 200-day average, at a new closing low, on high volume. The class read-through from the Summit letter is still fresh, with HARMONi-3 as a binary risk by year-end.
- Supportive: heavy cash, an active buyback (its average price was above the current price), and 2026 guidance raised. The buyback and cash floor have not stopped the slide.
- The $79.52 intraday low is the nearby support level. If it breaks, there is no obvious floor except the buyback.
- The only scheduled event inside the window is the possible HARMONi-3 or gotistobart interim news, both undated.

I stopped searching once new queries kept returning the same Q3 results and the same price moves. A few gaps remain, listed at the end. Search snippets and automated news sites carry most of the price and analyst figures, so check those against a live quote. The company filings and call summaries I opened are firmer.

## The story in one paragraph

The three stocks are a pricing-power trade, and each also has its own story. SHW and PPG pushed through large price increases in 2026. Middle East disruption (Strait of Hormuz) pushed up sulfur, TiO2, solvents and resin costs. Both reported Q3 on Oct 27-28 and narrowed their full-year guidance, which kept the midpoint but showed real price realization. Both also warned that 2027 demand will be soft, with no recovery in sight. ECL is a different story. It is an AI-data-center cooling growth story, helped by a Wells Fargo upgrade and a run of price-target raises this week. I found no news explaining why the basket has risen 6.4% over 20 sessions. The best I found is a rotation toward quality compounders plus the ECL catalysts, which is my inference. I also found no news today specific to any of the three names.

## SHW

- **Q3 (Oct 27):**
  - Sales were $6.86B, up 7.9%. Adjusted EPS was $3.63 against $3.59 a year earlier.
  - Gross margin fell to 47.8% from 49.2%, on raw-material and supply-chain costs plus dilution from Suvinil (the Brazilian paint business it bought).
  - Paint Stores same-store sales rose 3.9%. Volume was up low single digits and price up mid single digits. Segment margin slipped to 24.3% from 24.9%.
  - Consumer Brands adjusted margin fell to 18.3% from 23.3%. Roughly 70% of that decline is Suvinil.
  - Performance Coatings grew 8.8%, with a lower margin.
- **Guidance:** adjusted EPS $11.85–$12.15 (midpoint $12, unchanged). Q4 sales are guided up mid single digits.
- **Management tone:** "muted demand" through year-end and into 2027, "softer for longer", and no recovery assumed.
  - DIY is "bumping along the bottom".
  - Single-family completions fell high single digits in Q3.
  - The 8% Paint Stores price increase took effect Sept 1 and should reach normal realization in the first half of 2027.
  - 2027 raw-material inflation is guided at low to mid single digits, heaviest in the first half.
  - About $75M of cost savings are planned for 2027. A fuller 2027 outlook comes in January.
- **Stock:** the stock fell 2.7% on Oct 27, then rose 5.9% on Nov 2 with no identified cause. It was about $346 on Nov 18, trading at roughly 29-30x earnings (normalized P/E 29.1). Ex-dividend was Nov 13.
- **Analysts:** after Q3, Citi cut its target to $370 from $400 and Guggenheim cut to $375 from $400, both staying at Buy. UBS raised to $370 (Neutral). Consensus is about 15 Buy and 12 Hold, with an average target near $374, so the stock is about 8% below it.
- **Insiders:** two executives sold shares on Nov 3-4 at about $345.

## PPG

- **Q3 (Oct 28):**
  - Sales were $4.35B, up 7%, with organic growth of 5% (price +3%, volume +2%). This was the seventh straight quarter of organic growth.
  - Adjusted EPS was $2.25, up 6%.
  - Adjusted EBITDA margin was 18.2%, flat.
  - Performance Coatings organic sales rose 8%, with aerospace up double digits and backlog near $300M.
  - Architectural margin rose 300 bps to 24.0%, but its volume fell 2%.
  - Industrial EBITDA fell 11% and its margin fell to 14.4% because cost inflation ran ahead of index-based pricing. Full catch-up is not expected until Q1/Q2 2027. Automotive OEM sales were down.
- **Guidance:** full-year adjusted EPS of $7.90–$8.10, with the midpoint raised. Q4 is guided to low single digit organic growth, with margin flat to up 100 bps. Q4 cost inflation is guided at high single digits.
- **2027:** the CEO gave no guide until late January. He expects no "hockey-stick" recovery and would not count on price as a tailwind. Cost programs total about $100M over 2026-27.
- **Stock:** it rose 4.5% on Nov 2 to about $125, then fell 2.9% the next day. It was about $122-125 in mid-November, against a 52-week range of roughly $93–$133. It trades at about 15x earnings with a 2.8% yield, which is cheaper than SHW.
- **Analysts:** RBC and UBS both raised targets to $123 and both are neutral. The ratings split is about 9 Buy and 9 Hold. Ex-dividend was Nov 10.

## ECL

- **Q3 (reported about Oct 27):**
  - Sales were $4.69B, up 13%, with organic growth of 7% (price +5%, volume +2%).
  - Organic operating margin was 19.6%, up 70 bps.
  - Adjusted EPS was $2.18, up 5%. Reported EPS fell 5%. Net interest expense more than doubled, to $124.8M from $55.3M, because of acquisition financing.
  - Global High-Tech organic sales rose 63%. Life Sciences rose 17%.
- **Guidance:** 2026 adjusted EPS of $8.10–$8.20. Q4 organic sales growth of 6-7%. For 2027, the CEO expects organic growth at the upper end of the 5-7% target and a 20% adjusted operating margin.
- **Catalysts:**
  - The CoolIT Systems acquisition closed in July for about $4.75–5B. CoolIT makes direct-to-chip liquid cooling. The Ovivo ultra-pure-water business adds chip-fab water treatment.
  - Nov 13: Wells Fargo upgraded to Overweight and raised its target to $380 from $315. The target implies about 25% upside. The analyst estimates direct-to-chip cooling is under 20% penetrated. The stock rose 1.8% that day.
  - Nov 16: Ecolab launched an integrated AI data-center cooling platform. Nov 17: it launched an open AI-infrastructure ecosystem with Siemens, Alfa Laval and Dassault Systèmes. The same day it announced an expansion of its One Ecolab restructuring plan. I could not find the charge or savings figures.
  - Nov 18-19: Oppenheimer raised its target to $331 (outperform), Stifel to $356 (buy) and Baird also raised its target.
  - A director bought 600 shares on Nov 12 at $308.
- **Stock:** it opened at about $301-303 on Nov 18, up more than 16% year to date. The average target is about $332. About 21 of 26 analysts rate it buy.

## Backdrop

- **Market:** the S&P 500 had a five-day losing streak and sits about 6% below its early-October high. Today the market is rising on the Anthropic IPO debut, with tech leading. Brent is near $92 and cooling. September CPI was 3.7%, and a CPI release is due today. The 2-year Treasury yield rose to 4.83% on Nov 16 from 4.73% on Nov 10, which works against housing-sensitive names.
- **Basket versus XLB:** XLB was about $53 on Nov 11. I could not find its Nov 18 close. A tech-led rally today could explain some of the basket's lag against XLB.

## What this means for a 1-10 session trade

- **Case that the stretch continues:** the Q3 beats and raises, price realization and the ECL AI story are all fresh. Analyst target raises on ECL are still coming in.
- **Case for mean reversion:** the fundamental story for SHW and PPG did not improve after Q3, since both guided to a weak 2027 and SHW's target cuts were real. Insiders sold. SHW's valuation at about 30x is demanding. The basket is stretched 2.1 standard deviations above its norm against XLB, and today's session is already negative.
- **Near-term triggers:** today's CPI and the rate reaction, which matter most for SHW and PPG. Also the Freddie Mac mortgage rate (Thursdays), housing data, oil and Hormuz headlines, and the January 2027 guidance for SHW and PPG, which falls outside your window. No earnings fall inside the window.
- **The basket is not one story.** ECL's driver is idiosyncratic and AI-linked. SHW and PPG are housing and cost-inflation plays. A move in the basket could come from either side, and the three names may diverge.

## Gaps

- No cause found for the Nov 2 jump in SHW (+5.9%) and PPG (+4.5%).
- No XLB close for Nov 18.
- No current mortgage rate or today's CPI result.
- No figures for the ECL restructuring expansion.
- No PPG architectural volume outlook for 2027.

agents.report:
**CTVA research brief, as of 9:20 AM CT Thursday 2026-11-19**

CTVA is not a normal falling stock. It is the crop-protection remainder of Corteva after the seed business was spun off, and it just reset its earnings downward on Brazil. Some figures differ between sources, and I flag those below.

**1. What the ticker is now**
- Corteva spun off its seed and genetics business as Vylor (VYLR) on 2026-10-01, one Vylor share per Corteva share. CTVA fell about 84%, from $77.65 to $12.56, mechanically.
- Vylor trades in the high $60s to low $70s (post-debut price not confirmed). CTVA is now a pure crop-protection company: herbicides, some insecticides and fungicides, and biologicals. Its sales were about 44% of the old company.
- The new CEO is Luther Kissam, who joined in June 2026. Greg Page is chair. Chuck Magro went to Vylor as CEO.
- Index selling after the spin took another 5.2% off CTVA, per a trader-news site, so that figure is secondhand.
- Your screen's "prior 52-week low of $8.35" and the 50-day and 200-day averages of about $12 are built on post-spin prices. They are not distorted by the pre-spin $78 prices, but any feed that includes pre-spin history will be.

**2. The Q3 report on 2026-11-12 was the shock**
- The stock fell about 20-24% in the session. Sources disagree: $12.14 to $9.74 (RTT News, intraday) versus a close near $9.19 (Yahoo, and the 24.3% figure from KoalaGains).
- Adjusted EPS was $0.06 against about $0.09-0.10 expected. Net sales were $1.59B, down 9%, against roughly $1.77B consensus, a 10% miss.
- Adjusted EBITDA was $222M, down 17%.
- Full-year 2026 EBITDA guidance was cut to $1.10-1.125B from about $1.3B, which had been set at the September investor day. EPS guidance is $0.76-0.80.
- Management expects Q4 EBITDA to be about half of last year's, a margin of roughly 7-9%.
- Crop-protection pricing is now expected down mid-to-high single digits, versus low-to-mid single digits before.

**3. Brazil is the cause**
- Latin America organic sales fell 31%, with volume down 24% and price down 7%.
- Corteva carried about $250M of excess channel inventory from 2025 into the season. That is worth about $100M of full-year EBITDA.
- Another roughly $100M of the cut comes from market weakness and price erosion. Brazil sell-out is down about 12% year to date.
- Drivers cited: generics on late-life molecules, high interest rates, tight farmer finances, El Niño weather, and just-in-time buying.
- Conditions worsened sharply in the last two weeks of September, per Mizuho. That was right after the investor day.
- Credibility is the main bear point. Management called the Brazil channel "healthy" on the Q2 call, and the second-half growth it guided to did not happen.
- Outside Brazil the business grew: North America +7%, EMEA +12-14%, Asia Pacific +3-5%, and new-product volume +20%. US pricing fell 12% on generic acetochlor.

**4. Management's recovery case**
- Brazil channel inventory is expected to normalize by the end of this season, which will weigh on Q4.
- Pricing should be mostly aligned with channel prices by Q2 2027, and Brazil should improve year over year in the second half of 2027.
- Management expects 2027 growth from both cost and volume, but gave no formal guidance until the Q4 call, due around 2027-02-02.
- Cost actions: a third-party cost review, a hiring freeze, and some R&D projects paused for a year. Kissam said "we simply cannot afford the infrastructure we inherited."
- A restructuring of the manufacturing and partner network will cost about $130-140M in 2026 and run through 2028.
- Year-end cash is targeted at about $1.5B against about $1B of financial debt. Q4 is expected to consume cash. Buybacks are barred in Q4 by spin tax representations and are expected to resume in 2027.
- One commentary piece says management is reviewing a possible Brazil restructuring or exit. I saw that in a single source.

**5. Dividend**
- The first post-spin dividend is $0.05 per quarter, down from $0.18. It is payable 2026-12-15 to holders of record on 2026-12-01.
- That is about a 2.4% yield at $8.23. Barclays' article quotes 8.6%, which looks like a stale or trailing figure.
- One of the 8-K's cited sources says Barclays expects about 20% of free cash flow to go to dividends and 50% to buybacks.

**6. Analysts, mostly cuts after the report**

| Firm | Rating | Target |
|---|---|---|
| Oppenheimer | Downgraded to Perform | $17 target removed |
| RBC | Outperform | $11 (from $17) |
| Mizuho | not stated | $13 (from $16) |
| KeyBanc | Overweight | $14 (from $17) |
| Citi | Neutral | $10.30 (from $13.65) |
| UBS | Neutral | $10 (from $15) |
| Barclays | Equal-weight, reinstated | $11 |

- KeyBanc's view: about 6x EBITDA, a strong balance sheet, and about $450M of annual free cash flow at current EBITDA. It estimates 2026 EBITDA at $1.12B and 2027 at $1.139B, so it expects no 2027 rebound.
- Barclays expects 2029 EBITDA of about $1.35B, roughly $100M below company guidance.
- Ignore MarketBeat's "consensus target $48.83" and its moving averages. They mix in pre-spin prices.
- Barclays' reinstatement article carries a timestamp of "Nov 19, 3:18 PM" even though it is only 9:20 AM CT, so the time zone or timing is unclear. It cites a $8.36 price.

**7. Insider buying**
- CEO Kissam bought 32,292 shares on 2026-11-13 at an average of $9.30, about $300K. That took his holding up about 21% to 185,379 shares (MarketBeat).
- I could not confirm it from the SEC Form 4 itself. One search result said the Form 4 snippet was cut off.
- A report that Greg Page also bought is unverified.

**8. Legal overhang (PFAS)**
- Roughly 20 states and nine cities argued the spin was asset-shifting to dodge PFAS liability on legacy DuPont chemistry. One search result described a fraudulent-transfer suit by 15 states and Guam in Indiana, but the source I opened did not use that term.
- The Fourth Circuit reversed a lower-court order on 9/30, and the district court then refused to block the spin. The merits were not decided, and the case could run for years.
- A $455M North Carolina PFAS settlement (about $355M in present value, paid over 15 years) was shared among Chemours, DuPont and Corteva. It knocked CTVA down about 4.5% on the day.
- Under the 2021 cost-sharing deal, Corteva bears 29% of eligible EIDP legacy losses once thresholds are met. They were met by the end of 2025.
- I could not confirm how the spin changed Corteva's indemnification terms. That would need the 10-Q.
- The Q3 earnings release did not mention PFAS beyond generic risk language. Corteva says it has no PFAS judgments against it.

**9. Valuation, sentiment and price action**
- Market cap is about $5.6B and the stock trades near 6x EBITDA, so EV is roughly 6x on a roughly $1.1B base. KeyBanc's free cash flow figure implies an 8% yield on equity.
- The price went from about $9.2 on the 12th to $9.43 on 11/16, then to the $8.35-8.37 area on 11/18-11/19. Our $8.23 is a fresh low below that.
- I found no specific news explaining the slide after 11/16 beyond the analyst cuts and Barclays' reinstatement, so it looks like post-earnings drift and continued selling.
- Beta is 0.58 (MarketBeat). Debt to equity is 0.14.
- I found nothing on short interest.

**10. Setup for the 1-10 session window**
- **Bullish:** the stock is oversold (RSI 22) at about 6x EBITDA, and the CEO bought at $9.30. Several sell-side analysts still see $10-14 of value, and the business is clean and cash generative outside Brazil.
- **Bearish:** there is no catalyst until 2027-02-02. The next news is Brazil data, more cuts, or the PFAS case. Q4 is guided to be very weak, the guide has been missed before, and the trend is still down on light volume. The dividend was cut and the stock is making new lows below the old 52-week floor.
- **Unresolved:** I could not find any tax-loss or index-driven selling pressure specific to CTVA. The 12/1 dividend record date is inside the window's horizon, but the amount is small ($0.05).

**CORT: research summary as of 9:25 AM CT, Thu 2026-11-19**

**Bottom line:** CORT has fallen about 45% from its August peak. The selloff has three causes: a competitor's Phase 3 win, a flat guidance reaction after Q3, and insider selling. The business itself is strong and there is a binary FDA catalyst on Dec 17. I found no news dated Nov 17–19 explaining the latest leg down, so the stock looks like it is drifting lower with no new trigger.

**How the price got here**
- Dec 30, 2025: the FDA issued a complete response letter (CRL) on relacorilant for Cushing's syndrome (hypercortisolism). The stock fell about 50%. [Intellectia](https://intellectia.ai/news/stock/corcept-therapeutics-cort-shares-plunge-50-after-fda-complete-response-letter-on-relacorilant)
- Mar 25, 2026: the FDA approved relacorilant as Lifyorli for platinum-resistant ovarian cancer. This came about 3.5 months before its July 11 PDUFA date (the FDA's target decision date). Launch was Apr 1. [Drugs.com](https://www.drugs.com/history/lifyorli.html)
- Jul 30: after the Q2 report the stock rose 27%. It peaked at a $123.57 close on Aug 25 (the 52-week high you quoted is $126.38).
- Oct 23: Genmab's Rina-S (rinatabart sesutecan) hit its Phase 3 goals in platinum-resistant ovarian cancer, with a progression-free survival hazard ratio of 0.29 and a significant overall-survival benefit. CORT fell about 20%, from $107.50 to $85.86. No source states the cause explicitly, but the timing points to Rina-S. [GuruFocus](https://www.gurufocus.com/news/9140704/corcept-therapeutics-cort-shares-drop-20-on-genmabs-phase-3-success-in-ovarian-cancer) [Investing.com](https://in.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/why-is-corcept-therapeutics-stock-tumbling-today-93CH-5651984)
- Nov 3–4: Q3 beat estimates, but guidance was only reiterated and the stock fell about 8.6%, to a $74.88 close per Alphastreet. [Investing.com](https://ca.investing.com/news/earnings/corcept-therapeutics-falls-on-guidance-despite-earnings-beat-4927047)
- Nov 17: close of $70.07. [Trefis](https://www.trefis.com/stock/cort/articles/626179/what-is-driving-the-move-in-corcept-therapeutics-stock/2026-11-18)

**Q3 fundamentals** ([press release](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001088856/000162828026069494/cort110326ex991pressrelease.htm))
- Revenue was $340.5M, up 64% from a year earlier and up from $256.1M in Q2.
- Korlym plus its authorized generic brought in $249.1M. Lifyorli brought in $91.4M, up 92% from Q2. More than 2,300 patients and more than 1,700 physicians have used it, and management says use is shifting toward earlier lines of therapy.
- Net income was $126.8M and diluted EPS was $1.01. Operating margin was about 34%.
- Cash and investments are $662.3M, with essentially no debt.
- 2026 revenue guidance of $1.1–1.2B was reiterated, not raised, after several earlier raises. The call gave no explanation. Nine-month revenue is $761.5M, so guidance implies roughly $340–440M in Q4 by my arithmetic. That means the low end of guidance would be a sequential decline.
- Buybacks were $43.7M in Q3 but only $5.7M over the first nine months per the 10-Q. The two figures don't match, so I could not reconcile them.

**Catalysts in the 1–10 session window**
- **Dec 17 PDUFA for relacorilant in Cushing's.** The NDA was resubmitted Jun 17 with a global statistical analysis of glucose, weight and hypertension that management calls positive. The decision is 4 weeks out, so it is mostly outside a 1–10 session hold, but run-up and positioning could matter. [10-Q](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001088856/000162828026069501/cort-20260930.htm)
- **Dec 16:** summary judgment hearing in Teva's antitrust case against Corcept (N.D. Cal.). Trial is set for March 2027. A May 2026 ruling let most of Teva's claims survive dismissal. On Nov 9 Teva filed saying there is enough evidence for a jury. [Bloomberg Law](https://news.bloomberglaw.com/antitrust/teva-ruling-keeps-drug-monopoly-lawsuit-alive-against-corcept)

agents.report:
**Annaly (NLY) as of 8:55 AM CT, Thursday 2026-11-19**

**Summary.** NLY is a heavily levered agency mortgage REIT making new lows because rates are rising. The 10-year Treasury yield is above 5% and the market expects Fed hikes. The sell-off looks driven by rates and the Fed, not by anything specific to Annaly. Operations look sound. Earnings available for distribution (EAD) cover the dividend and insiders are buying. But book value is falling with rates, and no catalyst before the Dec 8-9 Fed meeting would obviously turn it.

**What happened**
- **Q3 results (Oct 20).** Book value fell 11.4%, from $20.15 to $17.86. Economic return was -7.6% and the GAAP loss was $(1.36) per share.
  - EAD was $0.80 against the $0.75 dividend, which beat estimates of about $0.77.
  - The release cites the 10-year yield rising 82 basis points. Management also cited wider agency MBS spreads and higher volatility; implied volatility hit an 18-month high in September.
- **Post-quarter book value.** Management said book value was up about 2% as of the Friday before the call, near 3% including the dividend accrual, and roughly flat since.
  - There is no official update since then. Yields have risen again and the stock made a new low, so book value is probably lower now. That is my inference, not a reported number.
  - At $16.78, the stock is about 0.94x the Q3 book value of $17.86.
- **Rates and the Fed.** The 10-year was about 5.06% on Nov 18, the 30-year 5.41%, and the 2-year about 4.80%.
  - Fed funds is 3.75-4.00%. The Fed held at the Oct 27-28 meeting by a 10-2 vote, and the minutes showed broad support for more hikes.
  - Governor Waller said a half-point hike is probably needed on Dec 8-9. Futures price about a 95% chance of a quarter-point hike.
  - Retail sales were stronger than expected. Oil and the Iran conflict are cited as additional drivers.
- **Mortgage rates.** Reports conflict. Freddie Mac's weekly 30-year rate fell to 7.11% in the week ending Nov 12. Daily lender trackers show rates up on the week, around 7.2-7.6%.
- **MBS spreads.** Morgan Stanley put the current-coupon spread at about +125 bps over Treasuries at the end of Q3, above its 10-year average of about +111. Annaly's call described spreads as near the widest since before mid-2025.
  - Management said new agency investments earn mid-to-high teens returns, and residential credit earns 13-16%.
  - I found no November spread data.

**The business**
- **Portfolio.** Economic exposure is $106.5B.
  - Agency MBS is 55% of capital ($91.8B).
  - Residential credit is 23% ($10.4B). The Onslow Bay securitization channel had record fundings of $5.8B.
  - Mortgage servicing rights are 22% ($4.3B). Servicing rights tend to gain when rates rise, which cushions the bond losses.
- **Leverage and hedging.** Economic leverage is 5.9x, up from 5.6x because equity fell. The hedge ratio is 100%.
  - Management is carrying slightly more duration and rate exposure than before. Early in Q4 it rotated over $2B into higher-coupon TBAs.
- **Liquidity.** Unencumbered assets are $6.9B, including $4.2B in cash and unencumbered agency MBS.
- **Margin.** Net interest margin excluding premium amortization adjustments was 1.69%, down 7 bps. Economic cost of funds rose to 4.03%.
- **Share issuance.** Annaly sold $757M of stock through its at-the-market program in Q3, and shares outstanding rose from 750.6M to 784.7M.
  - It used the money to redeem $442.5M of 6.75% Series I preferred on Oct 1 and to fund investments.
  - The sales were made above book value. At today's price, below book, issuing more would dilute holders, so a pause is likely. I found no November offering.
  - No buyback was announced.
- **Dividend.** The $0.75 quarterly dividend is unchanged. The Q3 yield was about 15.9% at the Q3 release's $18.89 price. At $16.78 it is about 17.9%.
  - Management expects to out-earn the dividend in Q4 but declined to project 2027.
  - The Q4 declaration has not happened. The ex-dividend date is projected for Dec 28-31, which falls after the Dec 8-9 Fed meeting.
- **Housing.** Management said that if mortgage rates stay near 7.4-7.5%, home prices could fall 2-4% nationally, and it called the Southeast "very weak." Serious delinquencies on servicing rights are under 60 bps.

**Price action and sentiment**
- NLY set a 52-week low of $16.72 on Nov 18 and closed at $16.94. Earlier lows came on Sept 30, Oct 6, Oct 19 and Nov 12.
- Analyst targets are mostly $19.50-22 and none were cut in November. The consensus is "Moderate Buy" with a $21.67 average target (1 strong buy, 7 buy, 3 hold, 1 sell). JPMorgan raised to $19.50 and Wells Fargo is at $22, both on Oct 22. TipRanks logged a neutral view with an $18.50 target on Nov 4.
- Director Scott Wede bought 50,000 shares at $18.80 (about $940K) on Nov 6, and the stock is now lower. CEO David Finkelstein sold 48,223 shares at $18.43 on Nov 2, and I did not find whether that was under a 10b5-1 plan. He also reportedly sold $1.1M around Sept 30.
- **Peers.**
  - AGNC's tangible book fell 16.9% to $7.13, and it trades at roughly 1.1x tangible book.
  - ARMOUR's book fell to $14.55. Its stock trades at about 0.75x book, and its early-November estimate was $15.52-15.62.
  - Orchid Island has cut its dividend twice, and AGNC has a history of cuts. Annaly's discount to book is the shallowest of these.
  - Annaly's EAD coverage is stronger than the 209.79% payout ratio on GAAP earnings suggests.

**For a 1-10 session trade**
- **For a bounce.** The stock is oversold at RSI 28. It is below book and sits at its low. Insiders and several analysts are constructive. Any softer inflation print or a drop in yields could lift book value and the stock quickly, since the book value per share moves with Treasury yields and MBS spreads. Bond-market pricing also already includes a 95% chance of a December hike.
- **Against.** The trend is firmly down, below falling 50-day and 200-day averages, and book value is probably still sliding. Yields are above 5% with a half-point hike being discussed, which would push spreads and book value lower. There is no company catalyst until the Jan 27 earnings report. Sector dividend-cut worries, a possible Annaly cut being priced in, and a pause in stock issuance are risks. Volume is normal, so there is no capitulation signal yet.
- **What to watch.** Daily moves in the 10-year yield and MBS spreads, any Annaly or peer book-value updates (ARMOUR posts these monthly), further Fed speakers, and inflation data before Dec 8-9. A halt to the Treasury sell-off matters more than anything Annaly itself does.

**Gaps.** I found no Annaly November book value estimate, no daily November MBS spread data, no Dynex or Two Harbors update, and no short-interest figure. Several figures came from aggregator pages with conflicting data; the primary numbers are from the 8-K and the call.

agents.report:
**SCCO: the story as of 8:57 AM CT, Thu 2026-11-19**

The selloff is mostly a sector and macro move in copper, not a company event. Southern Copper's Q3 report was strong on profit. The Q3 report did include a Tia Maria delay, and the stock fell far more after it than that news alone explains.

**Why it fell**
- **Copper broke down.**
  - LME 3-month copper hit about $13,019 to $13,027 a ton on Nov 18, its lowest since June 24.
  - The same piece says copper is heading for its longest run of weekly losses in two years.
  - It cites a stronger dollar ahead of the Fed minutes, upheaval in AI stocks, and a weak China outlook.
  - Zinc and nickel fell as well.
  - Copper was about $14,560 on Oct 29 and about $13,992 on Nov 10. [Yahoo/Bloomberg](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/commodities/articles/copper-extends-fall-near-five-051625319.html)
- **Copper is now treated as a barometer for the AI trade.**
  - An AI equity selloff erased about $2.5T from the Nasdaq 100.
  - Funds cut their net long CME copper position by about 58%, from 82,649 contracts in mid-September to 34,444.
  - The CME premium over LME fell from above $700 a ton in August to about $80. [Crux Investor, Nov 10](https://www.cruxinvestor.com/posts/ai-selloff-cut-coppers-us-premium-favoring-lme-priced-producers)
  - ING cautioned that the Nov 10 rebound might not end the correction.
- **Druckenmiller said he is short copper (Nov 17).**
  - He said the Fed is no longer cutting, commodities are weakening and credit spreads are widening.
  - He called the second half of 2027 potentially disappointing.
  - He added that he is "just taking a break, which could last two days or six months."
  - [PrimeXBT](https://primexbt.com/news/druckenmiller-says-he-is-short-copper-and-warns-of-economic-weakness-in-2027/) summarizes the remarks.
  - One Benzinga snippet says SCCO fell nearly 27% over the month. I could not open that page (403), so treat the figure as unverified. It is close to the 19.1% over 20 sessions our screen shows.
- **Peers fell in step.**
  - On Nov 16, SCCO fell 5.19%, Freeport fell 6.5%, and the sector fell 3.2%. [TradingKey](https://www.tradingkey.com/news/market-movers/262307645-market-movers-scco-20261116)
  - Another snippet had SCCO down about 6% in one session to about $146, with chipmakers and gold miners also weak. [GuruFocus](https://www.gurufocus.com/news/9202797/southern-copper-corp-scco-stock-down-62-now-undervalued-gf-score-95100)
  - BHP closed at its lowest since Apr 30, and Rio Tinto fell too. [Motley Fool AU](https://fool.com.au/2026/11/19/copper-price-falls-to-6-month-low-taking-rio-tinto-and-bhp-shares-with-it)
- **The stock carried a premium multiple.**
  - It trades near 21x to 22x forward earnings and about 14x EV/EBITDA, a premium to diversified peers.
  - Analyst average target is about $173, with a range of $136.60 to $272. That is from one article that also says "Hold" and "Reduce" in different places.
  - Earlier 2026 calls were bearish: UBS Sell with a $148 target, BofA Underperform, Barclays Underweight with a $148 target, and Itau BBA Underperform (dated Dec 2025 on the page).
  - I found no new rating change in November.
  - Simply Wall St's popular narrative fair value is $118 (an older page, quoted when the stock was $148).

**Company fundamentals (Q3 2026, reported around Oct 20; [TipRanks](https://www.tipranks.com/news/company-announcements/southern-copper-earnings-call-highlights-record-growth))**
- **Profit was strong.**
  - Sales were $4.7B, up 39%.
  - Adjusted EBITDA was $3.0B, a 65% margin.
  - Net income was $1.8B, up 63%.
  - Cash cost net of by-product credits was $0.09/lb.
  - The LME copper average was $6.41/lb.
- **Output is soft.**
  - Copper was 232,396 tons, down 1%, with Peru down 6% and Mexico up 2.5%.
  - Ore grades are lower in Peru.
  - 2026 guidance is 918,000 tons, and 2027 is slightly below 920,000.
  - Cost of operations rose 17%.
- **Tia Maria is later and may cost more.**
  - Start-up is now first half 2028, versus late 2027 before.
  - The project is 50% complete, with $884M spent.
  - Remaining capex is under review and may rise.
  - Peru revoked the permit in April and sent it for re-review. The ministry called that a review, not a cancellation. [Mining Weekly](https://www.miningweekly.com/article/peru-orders-new-review-of-southern-coppers-stalled-tia-maria-project-cancels-okay-2026-04-13)
  - El Pilar capex is up, with production now targeted for the second half of 2029.
  - Los Chancas has illegal miners on site and a possible construction start in the second half of 2028.
  - The Cuajone expansion is not approved.
- **Dividend.** The quarterly cash dividend is $1.30 per share, payable today, Nov 19, with a record date of Nov 3. The ex-date has passed, so it is already out of the price.
- **Parent.** Grupo Mexico trimmed its copper guidance in October. [Engineering News](https://engineeringnews.co.za/article/mining-giant-grupo-mexico-reports-higher-profit-on-price-boost-trims-copper-guidance-2026-10-21)

**What matters for a 1 to 10 session trade**
- **Why a bounce is plausible.**
  - RSI is 28, with Williams %R near 98 (oversold) on the Nov 16 snapshot, and funds have already cut length.
  - Earnings and cash flow are at records, and the dividend is paid.
  - The next report (Jan 26) is outside the window, so there is no event risk from earnings.
  - SCCO is near the $141 to $146 zone of its 20-day low.
- **Why it could keep falling.**
  - Copper is still breaking down, with no stabilization signal yet.
  - The dollar is firm, and Druckenmiller's macro caution may spread.
  - The AI-equity unwind is the main driver, and it is outside the company's control.
  - The valuation premium is still unwinding.
  - SCCO is below both the 50-day and 200-day averages.
- **Catalysts in the window.**
  - The Fed minutes, which I could not confirm.
  - AI and Nasdaq direction.
  - Any US refined-copper tariff news. A formal tariff would restore the US premium, but SCCO sells at LME-linked prices, so it benefits less than US-priced producers.
  - China data.
  - Peru and Mexico political headlines.

**Gaps**
- I found nothing on the Fed minutes outcome or on copper miners' premarket moves today.
- I found no stock reaction to the Q3 print on Oct 20 to 21.
- Several aggregator pages (TradingKey, GuruFocus, Simply Wall St) are low quality and contradict themselves on ratings and RSI.

**Bottom line.** SCCO is a high-beta copper proxy that is oversold in a copper selloff driven by macro and the AI unwind. Fundamentals are strong, and the Tia Maria delay is a smaller issue than the copper move. A bounce thesis depends on copper stabilizing near $13,000, and the stock has no company-specific reason to turn on its own.

agents.report:
**Bottom line:** The fall in TGB looks like a macro and copper-price move. I found no company-specific bad news. Q3 results were strong. The share price is falling with copper, and the Florence ramp is the open execution risk.

**Name and ticker.** Taseko renamed itself Trekor Metals on June 25, 2026, and the ticker TGB did not change. Some sources use "Taseko" and others "Trekor". Search for both.

**What the company reported**
- **Q3 release (about Nov 4–5):** Adjusted EBITDA was a record of about C$164M. The CFO cited C$161M and nobody reconciled the gap. Revenue was about C$342M, up from C$174M a year earlier. Net income was about C$34M, against a C$28M loss in Q3 2025.
- **Production:** Q3 copper output was about 41M lb, made up of about 34M lb from Gibraltar and about 7M lb from Florence. Gibraltar was its best quarter of the year, helped by higher-grade ore in the lower Connector Pit benches. Gibraltar's 2026 guidance was raised to 115–120M lb from 110–115M lb.
- **Balance sheet:** Cash was about C$214M and liquidity about C$400M. The revolver was extended to October 2029 and enlarged to US$130M. Net debt to EBITDA is about 1x, and management says debt reduction is a priority.
- **Earnings:** MarketBeat-style summaries say the reported EPS of $0.11 matched consensus. One summary instead said EPS of $0.15 missed. I couldn't settle this.

**Risks inside the story**
- **Florence ramp:** Florence is the Arizona in-situ copper project. Q3 output rose 35% quarter on quarter, but wellfield development is about three months behind plan. The company targets a full 7M lb per month run rate in early 2027. The 2026 Florence guide is 25–28M lb. In February it was 30–35M lb, so it has been cut. The company has missed guidance before. It cut its 2025 guidance in 2025 on weak Gibraltar recoveries.
- **Q4 at Gibraltar:** Management expects lower grades and recoveries as mining moves to the oxidized upper benches. A weaker Q4 is already flagged.
- **Costs:** Gibraltar's unit cost rose to $2.72/lb. Diesel and explosives add about $0.20–0.30/lb. Florence cost was US$3.54/lb, down about 25%, but acid costs are expected to rise in 2027 and the contract is not settled. Florence sustaining capital is about US$25M a quarter.

- **Copper:** Reports have copper down about 5–6% on Nov 18, to about $5.62/lb, its lowest since roughly April. It was about $6.50 in late October. Treat these as unverified: the sources are low-grade aggregators, and I couldn't confirm the claims about Fed hikes, a Druckenmiller short or Nvidia CEO news.

- **TGB on Nov 18:** It fell about 9.7% to about $5.57 from $6.21, with an intraday low of $5.49. That is your 20-day low. Put buying was about 182% above average (6,671 puts). The volume figure cited was below average.

- **Analysts:** Consensus is Moderate Buy, with five buys and one hold. The average target is about $9, and Jefferies initiated at Buy in August. I found no target cuts after Nov 18.

**For a 1–10 session trade**
- **Case for a bounce:** The business is at record earnings and the balance sheet is fine. The stock is far below the 50-day and 200-day averages, near a 20-day low, and has a small bid today. Consensus targets sit well above the price. Morgan Stanley was reported to call the copper selloff overdone.
- **Case against:** The stock is trading as a high-beta copper proxy (beta about 1.44). It will not turn until copper does, and I saw no sign copper has bottomed. Gibraltar's Q4 weakness is already signaled and Florence has a record of slipping. Heavy put buying shows hedging or bearish positioning.
- **Catalysts:** The next earnings release is roughly mid-February. Before then, the copper price and macro headlines decide the direction. I found no scheduled company event inside the window.
- **Read:** This is a copper-beta bounce trade. It is a reasonable candidate only if copper stabilizes. A fresh copper low means the stock likely breaks $5.49, and the 52-week low is $4.14.

**Bottom line:** ITUB's 28% drop over 20 sessions is mostly Brazil macro and currency, not a bank problem. The bank reported solid numbers on 11/3, and the stock rose about 3% in Brazil the next day. Today it is still trading near the lows with no bank-specific catalyst. The next scheduled catalysts are the lower-house fiscal vote (expected next week) and the Selic decision on 12/9. Earnings are not until 2027-02-03, so they are not a factor in a 1-10 session window.

**Why the stock is down**
- **Election shock:** Lula won the 10/25 runoff for a fourth term, beating Flávio Bolsonaro. Polls had favored Bolsonaro. On 10/26 the Brazil ETF fell about 25% premarket and the real dropped about 12%. Bovespa trading hit a circuit breaker.
- **Why it hit hard:** Analysts cited a 7-8% budget deficit, net debt near 70% of GDP, and campaign-period spending. Morgan Stanley expected a quick re-pricing of fiscal risk of about 200 bp. Bolsonaro initially refused to concede.
- **Prolonged slide:** The Ibovespa is about 19% below its 10/9 peak and down about 17% over 20 sessions. The dollar is up about 15% against the real over 20 sessions. The real hit a 12-month low of 5.78 per dollar on 11/16, and about 5.90 today.
- **11/16 leg down:** ITUB fell 5.31% in New York, the Brazil ETF (EWZ, a basket of Brazilian stocks) 4.03%, Vale 6.77% and Petrobras 5.67%. The Rio Times said it could not find a single trigger. Contributing factors were a US 10-year yield near 5.14%, the S&P 500 down 1.9% and the VIX up 19%. The real fell far more than the US dollar index rose.
- **Currency effect:** The ADR carries the real's fall on top of the local share price. The local share was about R$40.2 on 11/18, versus R$39.72 right after earnings. Much of the ADR's decline is the real, not the stock. Today's $6.78 is consistent with R$40 at about 5.9.
- **Selic:** On 11/4 the central bank held it at 13.75%, unanimously, ending five quarter-point cuts. Polymarket gave 82% to no change at the 12/9 meeting.
- **Fiscal package:** The Senate passed it on 11/18 (reported 69-2; earlier stages were 45-31 and 40-38). It targets up to R$60 billion of improvement in 2027, and the finance minister called it a "first step."
- **Lower-house vote:** The lower house, the Câmara, plans an extraordinary session Monday night, with a vote expected next week. The text could still be altered, and the IFI (the government's fiscal watchdog) said about 70% of the package's revenue is uncertain.
- **Today:** The Ibovespa was roughly flat to up about 0.3% near 168,000. The dollar hit about R$5.91. Itaú BBA downgraded its Brazil view (growth, inflation and rates worsening) while keeping a 195,000 Ibovespa target for 2027. ITUB4 traded slightly lower.

**The bank itself (3Q26, reported 11/3)**
- **Results:** Recurring net income was R$12.6 billion, up 2.5% from the prior quarter and 6-7% from a year earlier. Sources disagree on the exact year-over-year figure. Recurring ROE was 23.6%, down from 24.3% in 2Q26.
- **Credit:** Cost of credit was about 2.7% of the portfolio (about R$10.4 billion), described as stable. The CEO said he has "excess comfort" on provisions. Capital (CET1) was 12.7%. The effective tax-rate guidance was cut to 28-29%.
- **Cautious notes:** The CEO said there was oversupply of credit, and 2027 will be challenging whoever won. He listed slowing activity, rising unemployment, high household debt, inflation near 6% and restrictive rates for a long time. He expects tougher wholesale credit in 2027, and ROE may be somewhat lower. There is no ROE guidance, and early-year guidance will come later. The bank is deliberately giving up card market share, and raised its cost-of-capital assumption to 15.25% from 14.5%.
- **Payouts:** Dividends follow the existing policy of paying out capital above 12% CET1. A buyback of up to 200 million preferred shares runs through August 2027. Itaú announced R$3.85 billion in interest on capital (JCP) in March. A dividend aggregator reported later payments, but I could not verify them.
- **Analysts:** All still rate it a buy as of 11/18. Targets are in reais: BTG R$54 (R$53 on its dashboard), Genial R$54.70, XP R$50 (calls it a top sector pick), BB Investimentos R$50, and a consensus near R$47.9 of uncertain date. UBS BB cut its target without disclosing the new one. Seu Dinheiro says analysts diverge on upside.
- **Reaction to results:** One source said the numbers were slightly below projections, another that credit quality beat. The net read is that it was in line.

**Read for a 1-10 session trade**
- **Case for a bounce:** The fundamentals are intact and RSI is 32. The 52-week low of $6.57 is only about 3% below. A fiscal vote that passes, or a firmer real, would likely lift the ADR. The Rio Times noted that after six similar Ibovespa falls, the index was higher 20 sessions later in four cases.
- **Case against:** The trend is down, the price is below its 20-day low and both moving averages, and the real is making new lows. The risk is two-sided around the fiscal vote.
- **Other risks:** There is global risk-off (US yields above 5%, a US rate hike priced for 12/9, AI-stock volatility, US-Iran tension). An amended or failed vote would hit the real.
- **Position size:** The ADR moves with the currency, so the stop should be set with that in mind.

**Gaps**

- Several pages disagree on exact levels (the dollar, Ibovespa, year-over-year growth). The Rio Times pieces were internally inconsistent.

# US refiners (MPC, VLO, PSX, PBF, DINO, DK, CVI, PARR): research as of 9:25 AM CT, Thu 2026-11-19

## Bottom line

The group is in a sharp, justified de-rating, and the screen's "stretched, no turn yet" reading is mostly the market repricing a collapsing gasoline crack. This is not a dip with a missing catalyst. Fundamentals are still very strong in absolute terms, so a bounce is plausible. But the main driver, the gasoline crack, has not stopped falling, and I found no catalyst that would force a turn in 1-10 sessions.

I could not open the IEA report, the Rigzone piece or the Invezz piece (403 errors). The Invezz piece's claim that Trump's Iran strike threat has returned is unverified. Several details come from aggregator summaries and are flagged below.

## The story

**1. The 2026 boom came from a product-supply shock.**
- The Iran war and the Hormuz disruption took more than 4-5 million b/d of refining capacity offline, split between the Middle East and Russia (HF Sinclair and PBF management).
- Ukrainian drones hit Russian refineries, and Russia banned diesel exports.
- China curtailed product exports.
- Global product inventories are depleted. PBF cited roughly 500 million barrels below pre-war levels.
- The US 3-2-1 crack averaged about $68 in September, the highest since 2006. The diesel crack topped $100 a barrel, and US retail diesel hit about $6.32.
- Q3 results were records:
  - VLO refining margin $39.24 a barrel, net income $6.8B.
  - MPC adjusted EPS $26.93, 100% utilization.
  - PSX adjusted EPS $14.08, 98% utilization.
  - PBF EPS about $12.5, DINO $11.75, PARR $10.70 adjusted, CVI $4.00 adjusted.
- Refining and marketing was the best S&P 500 subindustry of 2026, up about 145% through September. VLO was up about 114% year to date, with a 52-week high of $459.78 on Oct 14.

**2. The unwind has been two legs.**
- **Leg one, Oct 27:** VLO fell about 8-9%, MPC 6.7-7.4% and PSX 6.5-7%. Benzinga read it as a repricing of the crack on Iran talks and the first Russian diesel cargo to the US, not a crude move. WTI fell only 1.8% that day.
- **Leg two, Nov 17-18:**
  - VLO fell about 5.5% to about $344.61.
  - MPC fell about 5.2% to about $377.
  - PSX fell about 4.7% to about $246.
  - DINO fell 7.3%.
  - PBF fell 7.1% to $62.39, down about 26% in a month, on light volume.
  - Trefis said the other seven refiners over $2B in market cap had a median drop of 7.2%.
  - XLE fell 3.3% and the S&P energy sector fell 3.5%.
  - Trefis found no company news behind VLO's move.
  - VLO was down about 21% over the past month, about 25% below its high.

**3. The proximate driver is the gasoline crack, not diesel or crude.**
- The US 3-2-1 crack fell about 36% in six weeks, from $65.56 on Oct 9 to about $41.90 on Nov 18 (James Thorne, Bloomberg, via Syz). That is a fresh low.
- Wholesale gasoline is down about 20%. Nearly all of the drop is gasoline, which weakens after the driving season.
- Diesel margins have barely moved and are still about three times normal.
- Thorne's cause: fat margins pushed refiners to run flat out, and products now flood the market.
- Retail gasoline is about $3.75 versus $4.30 a month ago. Retail diesel is about $5.94.
- Heating oil/ULSD closed about $3.97 on Nov 18, below its 200-day average, and RBOB is about $2.48 (one aggregator, unreliable).
- Crack figures vary by source, roughly $41-45.

**4. Crude and macro backdrop.**
- WTI closed at $83.26 on Nov 18, its lowest since Aug 26, and is down about 20% in November. Brent is about $92. WTI was near $100 in late October.
- The IEA now sees a Q4 surplus of about 1.7-2 million b/d. Goldman sees a large surplus into 2027.
- EIA report for the week ended Nov 13, released Nov 18:
  - Crude rose 3.4M barrels to 417.8M.
  - Gasoline rose 5.2M to 215.9M, 3% above the 5-year average.
  - Distillates rose 1.6M to 104.9M, 7% below the 5-year average.
  - Refinery utilization was 95.7%.
  - Gasoline stocks are above average and distillate stocks are below. That matches the gasoline-down, diesel-firm split.
- Offsetting this, Hormuz shipping attacks continue and Iran's navy said three tankers hit mines. Ukrainian strikes have cut Russian refinery runs about 45% since late October (ANZ, via CNBC). Diplomacy is stalled and a third US carrier has arrived.
- Rate risk: the 10-year yield is about 5.07%, and the Fed is expected to hike in December. Waller floated 50 basis points.
- The S&P 500 has fallen five straight sessions, down nearly 4%.

**5. Management and street view.**
- **Management on duration:**
  - VLO says current cracks are "very sustainable". It argues Asian refiners earn only $2-3 a barrel and that European gas costs put a floor under cracks.
  - MPC expects an enhanced mid-cycle environment through at least mid-2027.
  - DINO's CEO says full product recovery is unlikely before 2028.
  - PBF expects margins to stay elevated and volatile.
- **Dissent:**
  - Jefferies downgraded VLO and MPC to Hold on Sept 22 (targets $401 and $413), warning that prices already implied a rich mid-cycle margin.
  - Bank of America said most offline capacity could return quickly if the strikes stop.
  - Morningstar calls the group overvalued even after the margin rise.
- **Ratings and targets:**
  - MPC: Mizuho cut its target to $440 (neutral) on Nov 16, Zacks downgraded to Hold on Nov 13, the consensus target is about $424, and a Nov 19 article cites insider selling.
  - DINO: five buys, none selling, median target about $130 (range $110-152). The CEO bought 25,000 shares, and a $233M repurchase from a large holder was reported.
  - DK: Zacks named it Bull of the Day on Nov 18 (Rank #1), citing upward estimate revisions. Its main risk is easing of the conflict.

**6. Company specifics.**
- **MPC:** Selling the St. Paul Park and Mandan refineries for $4.2B, closing by the end of Q4, with proceeds to go to the Gulf Coast. Capture was 93%.
- **VLO:** Q4 throughput guidance of 2.875-2.975M b/d, lower than Q3. Q4 opex guidance is about $4.85 a barrel. Next earnings are in January.
- **PSX:** Q4 utilization guided to the mid-90s, with turnaround expense of $140-170M. Q4 will weight toward buybacks to reach the 50% payout target. Coastal Bend pipeline expansion starts moving volumes in Q4.
- **PBF:**
  - Net cash after redeeming $800M of notes. Gross debt is about $1.4B and interest savings are at least $130M in 2027.
  - Q4 throughput guidance of 925-985k b/d with no turnarounds. The 2027 turnaround schedule is heavy.
  - Dividend raised 18% to $0.325.
  - Most levered to cracks and West Coast. Torrance had an emergency flaring filing.
- **DINO:**
  - Q4 crude charge guided to 560-600k b/d because of the El Dorado turnaround.
  - About $600M of the quarter's benefit is a deferred small-refinery RINs waiver, not current cash.
  - Mississauga is being shut. The Westline decision slipped to Q1 2027.
  - Opex is rising.
- **CVI:**
  - Q3 adjusted EPS $4.00, but GAAP $5.67 includes a $314M RFS liability benefit from the Wynnewood waiver.
  - RIN costs of $11.20 a barrel cut capture about 16%.
  - Dividend of $0.10 was paid Nov 23 to holders of record Nov 16.
  - It trades on RINs and its fertilizer segment as well as cracks.
- **PARR:**
  - Adjusted EBITDA $646M, including a $222M small-refinery exemption gain, so the underlying run rate is lower.
  - First net cash position.
  - Hawaii turnaround is done.
  - Q4 throughput guidance is about 200k b/d system-wide. Hawaii and Rockies differentials are the swing items.
  - It has the least beta to the US Gulf Coast crack, which fits it being today's best name.

**7. Policy risk.**
- Late September: Trump seriously considered a 90-day diesel export ban. Early October reporting says the White House ruled out a blanket ban and pivoted to red-diesel, excise-tax and RFS options and voluntary export cuts.
- I found nothing newer. Midterm pressure and a high diesel price keep this a live tail risk for the Gulf Coast names (VLO, MPC, PSX), though diesel prices are now falling.
- The Jones Act waiver expired Nov 15.

## What this means for the one-to-ten-session decision

- **Case for a bounce:**
  - The group is down about 15% against XLE in 20 days and has hit 2 standard deviations below its norm.
  - Q3 earnings are enormous and buybacks are ongoing.
  - Valuations are about 0.64 times sales for VLO.
  - Diesel cracks remain extreme.
  - Management says margins are durable.
  - Crude is steadying near $83 and Hormuz risk persists.
  - A relief rally in a crowded 2026 winner is plausible.
- **Case against catching it:**
  - The leading indicator, the gasoline crack, is still falling and at a new low.
  - Gasoline stocks just built 5.2M barrels.
  - An IEA and Goldman surplus narrative is in place.
  - The group is still up about 100% year over year, so profit-taking has room to run.
  - A Fed hike and a falling S&P add pressure.
  - Any Iran ceasefire headline would push capacity back online and cut the crack further, and Oct 27 showed refiners fall about 3-4 times as hard as crude on that kind of news.
  - Dispersion is likely: refiners with heavy-crude, RINs or West Coast exposure (PBF, DK) can swing most.
- **Things to watch:**
  - The daily RBOB and ULSD cracks.
  - The EIA report on Nov 25 (gasoline stocks).
  - Iran and Hormuz headlines.
  - Any diesel export restriction news.
  - MPC's asset-sale close.
  - Hold-rating and target changes.
  - Fed expectations.

## Source quality caveats

- Prices and percentage drops differ across sources. MarketBeat's dollar drops and Trefis's percentages do not reconcile.
- Crack figures vary by aggregator, and the Zacks and Defense World items are thin.
- I did not find today's price action (Nov 19 regular session) beyond the screen data you gave.

**BBWI research, Thursday 2026-11-19, about 9:00 AM CT**

**Bottom line:** The news that explains this week's slide is already out. Bath & Body Works (BBWI) reported before the open today and beat on the quarter. The weak part was a fourth-quarter EPS guide below consensus. The stock opened near $18.68 and is now $18.34, so today's move is a mild fade, not a crash. I found no post-earnings analyst notes, no call transcript and no reliable account of today's reaction. Treat the market's verdict on the report as unconfirmed.

**What happened today (Q3 FY2026, quarter ended Oct 31)**
- **Sales:** $1,577M, down 1.0%, against consensus of about $1.55B. The company said it beat its own guide of down 2.5% to 5%.
- **EPS:** Adjusted EPS was $0.26, against $0.12 expected. Guidance had been $0.07 to $0.12. The year-ago figure was $0.35. Reported EPS was $0.19.
- **Channels:**
  - U.S. and Canada stores: comps down 4.3% (year to date down 4.7%).
  - Direct (digital): up 2.6%, the second straight quarter of growth.
  - International and other, which includes wholesale: up 39.3%.
- **Margins:** Gross margin was 40.5% against 41.3% a year ago. Adjusted operating income was $121M, about 7.7% of sales.
- **Full-year guidance:**
  - Sales outlook raised to down 2.1% to 3.4%, from down 2.5% to 4%.
  - Adjusted EPS held at $2.60 to $2.80 (consensus about $2.56 to $2.74, depending on source).
  - Free cash flow about $600M.
- **Q4 guidance (the negative):**
  - Sales down 2.0% to 5.5%, against about down 2.7% expected.
  - EPS $1.41 to $1.61, against $1.72 consensus.
  - Last year's Q4 was $2.05 adjusted.
- **Tone:** CEO Daniel Heaf said the company is "taking a prudent view of the consumer environment" for the holidays. He also said "progress will not always be linear."
- **Wholesale timing:** MarketBeat's summary has management saying some Q4 revenue shifted into Q3 because of wholesale shipments to Ulta and Amazon. That is a secondary source. If true, part of the Q3 beat borrowed from Q4.
- **Capital:**
  - New $500M buyback, but it starts only after the existing January 2025 program is finished. Year-to-date buybacks were just $59M, against $344M a year earlier.
  - Long-term debt fell to $3.37B from $3.89B. Cash is $318M.
  - $0.20 quarterly dividend, about a 4.3% yield. **Ex-dividend date is tomorrow, Nov 20** (payable Dec 4), so expect a mechanical drop of about $0.20 (about 1.1%) at tomorrow's open.

**Why the stock was already weak before the print**

agents.report:
**KBR research summary as of 9:00 AM CT, Thursday 2026-11-19**

**The setup.** KBR looks stretched because of the Trinzic spin-off, not because of an earnings problem. The Q3 report was fine and guidance was kept. The selloff came after the Investor Day on Nov 11-12.

**Business and Q3 (reported Oct 29)**
- Revenue was $2.03B, up 5% and about $10M under consensus. Adjusted EPS was $1.12 against $1.00 expected, up from $1.02 a year earlier. Net income was $133M, up 16%. Adjusted EBITDA was $268M, up 12%.
- Sustainable Technology Solutions (STS) revenue rose 26% to $762M, with a record $5.8B backlog. Plaquemines LNG contributed about $115M in Q3 and is expected to add $25-35M in Q4.
- Mission Technology Solutions (MTS) revenue fell 5% to $1.27B, mainly from NASA insourcing. Its adjusted EBITDA rose 5%.
- FY26 guidance was reaffirmed: revenue $7.90-8.36B, adjusted EBITDA $980M-1.04B, adjusted EPS $3.87-4.22, adjusted operating cash flow $560-600M.
- Management said Middle East collection delays could push $25-50M of cash past year-end, and cash flow is weighted to Q4.
- Net leverage was 2.1x.

**The spin-off**
- MTS becomes Trinzic, Inc., targeted for Jan 4, 2027, subject to final board approval and customary conditions. Trinzic would launch with more than $5B of revenue and a $17.3B backlog. Michael LaRouche is CEO-designate.
- Trinzic's 2027-29 targets are 3-6% revenue growth (excluding NASA insourcing) and an adjusted EBITDA margin of 9% or better. They also include more than $700M of cumulative operating cash flow and net leverage of 2.5x or less.
- Expected net leverage at separation is about 3.15x. That is a heavy balance sheet for a low-margin government services company.
- The 2027 NASA insourcing headwind is about 4%. About 80% of 2027 revenue is under contract. Trinzic's dividend policy is still undeveloped.
- On Nov 18, subsidiary Solar MTS Holdings launched a $500M senior notes offering tied to the spin. Debt financing is a near-term event, and I could not find the pricing.
- RemainCo KBR is mainly the STS business. Its targets are 10%+ organic revenue CAGR from 2026 to 2029 and a 12%+ adjusted EBITDA margin for 2027-29. They also include free cash flow conversion of 85% or better, and net leverage under 2.5x. The company says these are objectives, not guidance, and they exclude megaprojects.
- The company gave no EPS target and no buyback amount.
- One secondary report gives about $3.85B of 2029 revenue and more than $425M of EBITDA for RemainCo. A second report calls the $425M a separation baseline, so that figure is unclear.

**Price action and likely cause**
- KBR closed at $38.65 on Nov 9. It fell about 6.7% on Nov 11 to roughly $36.3, then fell about 4% more on Nov 12-13. It is now about $32.4-32.9, and Wednesday's close was $33.08. The 52-week low is $29.67-29.94 and the high is $44.76-45.37.
- Several sources attribute the Nov 11-12 drop to the Investor Day targets. I could not find a dated post-event write-up that explains it. A plausible reading is that the 3.15x leverage, Trinzic's modest growth and margins, and the lack of EPS or buyback detail disappointed. That is my inference, not something a source stated.
- This is the third sharp drop on a spin-related event this year. The Sept 2025 spin announcement, the Dec 2025 Lake Charles LNG suspension, and the Q1 and Q2 prints each produced drops of 5-8%. The stock is down about 45% year over year, driven by government contract losses (the HomeSafe cancellation), NASA insourcing, and weak free cash flow.
- The stock's decline has been steady rather than a one-day collapse. Forced selling around a spin-off and index changes is a common pattern, but I found no source confirming it here.

**Valuation and analysts**
- Forward P/E is about 8.3 and trailing P/E about 9.3. Market cap is about $4.5B and beta is 0.42.
- MarketBeat shows a Hold consensus, with an average target of $44.83 and three Buy and five Hold ratings. Stockanalysis shows Buy from 8 analysts, with an average target of $44.86.
- The latest target changes are Wells Fargo $40 (equal weight, Nov 2) and Citi $48 from $49 (Buy). Older ones are Oppenheimer $50 from $60 (outperform, Sept 22), UBS $41 (neutral, Aug), and BofA $40 (neutral, July). I found no target cuts clearly tied to the Investor Day.
- The dividend is $0.165 a quarter, a yield of about 1.8%. The ex-dividend date is Dec 15, which is after the 1-10 session window.
- Institutions own about 97% of shares. Boston Partners added to its stake in Q3.

**Catalysts and risks over the next 1-10 sessions**
- **Possible upside:**
  - The notes offering prices smoothly.
  - Analysts defend the stock, since its valuation is low and the average target is about 38% above the price.
  - The stock bounces off its 52-week-low area of about $29.7-29.9.
- **Possible downside:**
  - The debt terms come in worse than expected.
  - Spin-related selling continues into the Jan 4 date.
  - There is further news on NASA or government procurement.
  - The weak market reaction to the Investor Day persists.
- **Missing information:** I found no news from Nov 14-19 explaining the further drift lower. I also found no short interest figure, no insider activity this month, and no pricing for the notes. The 5-day and 20-day declines your screen shows fit a slow slide with no new negative earnings news.

**Verdict for the journal.** There is no fundamental break, but a clear reason for investors to sell. The stock is below its 20-day low with no confirmed turn, and the spin date is about six weeks away. A rebound trade is a bet that the overhang from the spin is priced in. The notes pricing is the nearest catalyst to watch.
